title: Make One-Star summon and synthesis lifecycle atomic
description: Latest playtest one-star-human-test-death event 63 declared five premium summons but only activated Rowan and Renna, spawned no other records, and even described the three missing cards as only a couple of bodies. Event 64 then silently replaced the Master's explicit named synthesis sources with those nonexistent anonymous Heroes, invented an up-to-three source cap to protect established names, reported permanent consumption with cull empty, and claimed Rowan advanced while his mechanics stayed empty. This corrupts canonical roster truth, overrides the player's lethal choice, and removes every threatened Hero's authored opportunity to react.
design: Add the smallest One-Star-specific transactional adjudication boundary for roster-changing management operations. Every acquired Hero must resolve to exactly one existing activation or durable spawn record. Synthesis must reference real source ids, preserve the submitted selection or request a valid narrower choice, expose the authored interruptible procedure before irreversible resolution, cull the exact consumed ids, and record target advancement atomically. Generic schemas may validate referenced lifecycle ids, but gacha prices, caps, and formulas must remain outside the rules-neutral narrative engine. Coordinate exact resource/facility state with ayoa-1uhz rather than duplicating a second ledger.
acceptance_criteria: A five-summon operation yields exactly five durable activated/spawned people with identities before any can be selected or rendered as material. A synthesis attempt cannot consume ambient or nonexistent people, silently substitute protected names, or invent a cap; successful resolution culls the exact selected source ids and durably advances the target exactly once, while cancellation/failed adjudication changes nothing. Threatened autonomous Heroes receive the story's actionable response boundary before permanent consumption. Invalid lifecycle output fails or retries before broadcast/persistence. Offline tests cover acquisition, selection, interruption, atomic success/rollback, checkpoint reload, and non-One-Star isolation.
notes: Absorbed by the One-Star adapter: summon costs and exact spawn/activate identities apply atomically; invalid or partial batches roll back; synthesis references exact real IDs, waits behind the pending/Cat-II response boundary, culls exact sources, requires monotone target improvement, and is idempotent across retries/reload.
close_reason: Summon and synthesis lifecycle is now exact, staged, atomic, rollback-safe, and idempotent.

title: Generate remaining seeded cast and veiled one-star sprite sweeps
description: Extend the reviewed Mirelle/Rowan pose-expression proof across every remaining seeded One-Star Ascension visual identity and create the reusable blurred-face one-star defaults. This remains a controlled asset experiment: no production registry, checkpoint, engine prompt, or on-the-fly generation change until the user reviews and locks the packs.
design: Generate the same coordinated neutral, happy, concerned, tense, skeptical, angry, sad, and surprised pose-expression sweep for Aveline Morcant, Castor Valebrand, Halcyon, Iselle, Liora Fen, Renna Holt, Seris Nightglass, Soren Ironvow, Veil the Unnumbered, the Warden of the Eighth, and Wren. Use each approved locked multi-view/reference set with explicit exclusions preserved. Wren is a hard exception: use app/storage/stories/one_star_ascension_s1/visual-references/wren_thelantern.png as the primary source and never use locked/wren_thelantern/active_profile.png because its kneepads are rejected. Never use Soren original rejected top-level art. Generate one masculine and one feminine blurred one-star default, each with the eight readable body-language poses; keep faces deliberately and consistently obscured, clothing basic, and identities non-specific. Keep canvas, baseline, scale, transparency, and dialogue-safe framing compatible with the proof pack. Use built-in generation for new base pose candidates under the established imagegen workflow. For visible signature props, compare against a manually chosen canonical prop crop/reference; use the repo Qwen Image Edit path as a targeted second-pass repair when consistency fails, with the candidate as edit target and prop reference as supporting input. Prefer the masked prototype endpoint for localized edits and reject whole-image drift. The Qwen gateway must be health-verified on 127.0.0.1:8199 and restored through the documented four-worker MI210 path if unavailable; do not silently substitute FLUX img2img or modify .env. Preserve raw/rejected/corrected artifacts, exact prompts, hashes, per-character contact sheets, and manual review.
acceptance_criteria: The experimental review pack contains eight normalized RGBA pose-expression candidates for each of the eleven remaining seeded identities plus eight masculine and eight feminine veiled defaults, with per-character contact sheets and one complete cast overview. Wren provenance proves the exact top-level wren_thelantern.png hash was used and the active-profile hash was absent from every job. Soren prohibited-source checks pass. Every character is graded for identity, hair, outfit, anatomy/hands, prop ownership/count/design, transparency, baseline/framing, and expression/pose semantics. Qwen repair records name primary target, supporting prop reference, endpoint/model, prompt, mask/bounds when used, before/after hashes, and rejection decision; edits cannot silently replace a better original. Blurred defaults remain generic, visually intentional, stable across all eight poses, and contain no seeded facial identity. All assets remain unlocked/unbound, the prior Mirelle/Rowan pack remains byte-identical, Windows Pictures/Ayoa review copies hash-match tracked files, validation/relevant tests pass, and the isolated branch is committed and pushed.

title: Add a prompt-independent deterministic VN sprite compositor
description: Build the generic engine path that can place zero, one, or two already-resolved transparent character sprites over an immutable visual-novel stage. This slice must not decide how an LLM selects pose-expression labels and must not generate or bind Mirelle/Rowan assets; it establishes the reusable composition, provenance, persistence, and delivery contract using synthetic fixtures.
design: Trace the existing VisualNovelDeckSection, compositor, presentation manifest, EngineBridge, CLI, and Discord delivery paths before editing. Add one rules-neutral ordered sprite-placement contract carrying only opaque resolved identity/variant provenance plus deterministic layout inputs such as slot, facing, anchor, and scale. Resolve and hash-validate bytes outside LLM inputs, alpha-composite sprites after the stage and before dialogue UI, and bind ordered sprite hashes and transforms into deck/card identity. Preserve identical card bytes across restart and shared CLI/Discord delivery. Support background-only, one-sprite, and two-sprite cards; maintain stable baseline and safe dialogue-box overlap. Keep One-Star reveal rules, dynamic generation, model prompts, expression semantics, and production asset registries out of this slice. Retire any redundant parallel DTO introduced during implementation rather than adding compatibility shims.
acceptance_criteria: Offline synthetic fixtures prove zero, one, and two sprites; inward-facing left/right placement; different per-page resolved variants; alpha edges; stable scale/baseline; correct layer order beneath dialogue UI; immutable approved background preservation; and deterministic card/deck identity. Manifest/load/restart rejects missing, tampered, symlinked, malformed, or mismatched sprite sources before unsafe delivery. CLI and Discord use the same manifest-verified rendered bytes and accessible text remains unchanged. No runtime LLM prompt, image-generation request, One-Star rule, production reference binding, or Mirelle/Rowan asset is changed. Focused and full proportional tests, Ruff, compile, diff checks, commit, and push are required.

title: Prototype Mirelle and Rowan pose-expression sprite packs
description: Before changing runtime sprite-generation prompts, prove a controlled asset workflow on two locked seeded identities: Mirelle Voss and Rowan Kest. Produce transparent visual-novel character cutouts for the agreed core emotional sweep, with body language and pose changing meaningfully alongside the face rather than reusing one rigid pose. First-pass failures are expected and must be preserved as evidence instead of silently replaced.
design: Use the locked active-profile, facial-zoom, anatomy, and back-view references as identity inputs after manually inspecting them. Follow the built-in image-generation skill: pilot a small discriminating subset first, inspect every output, then iterate with one targeted correction before expanding. The core sweep is neutral, happy, concerned, tense, skeptical, angry, sad, and surprised; each variant should use emotion-appropriate head angle, shoulders, hands, weight distribution, and relationship to the character weapon while keeping canonical identity, hairstyle, outfit, colors, anatomy, and weapon ownership fixed. Additional character-signature variants may be proposed separately, but do not silently redefine the core labels. Use consistent transparent canvas dimensions, ground/baseline, scale, three-quarter VN framing, and safe lower dialogue-box occlusion. Preserve exact prompts, reference hashes, output hashes, rejection reasons, and overview sheets. Keep all candidates experimental: no checkpoint/reference-registry binding, no runtime prompt changes, and no production approval claim.
acceptance_criteria: A review pack contains eight attempted pose-expression variants for Mirelle and eight for Rowan, plus preserved rejected iterations where applicable. At least one overview shows each complete sweep at readable size. Manual review grades identity, face, hair, outfit, anatomy/hands, weapon count/ownership, transparency/edge quality, pose legibility, framing/baseline, and semantic distinction. Final candidates contain one character only, no environment, text, logo, watermark, duplicate person, or extra weapon. Prompts and a conflict audit explain how pose variation was requested without redesigning the character. Files and manifests are hash-pinned, copied to a clearly named Windows Pictures/Ayoa review folder, committed and pushed on an isolated branch, and explicitly remain unlocked pending user selection.
notes: User review, 2026-08-26: regenerate Mirelle concerned and tense. Use each current Mirelle sprite as the primary edit target in a localized Qwen Image Edit pass with one manually selected canonical spear reference so the same spear design is preserved across the whole Mirelle sweep; reject any edit that changes face, pose, hair, outfit, proportions, or transparency outside the prop repair. Regenerate Rowan sad and verify both mismatched knives against its canonical reference. Preserve every prior candidate and write v2 siblings; do not overwrite or lock.

title: Reveal One-Star identities through promotion-ready sprite packs
description: A dynamic summon cast cannot rely on a permanently pre-authored sprite for every Hero. Turn that constraint into One-Star fiction: from the Master viewpoint, every birth-one-star Hero initially uses a stable generic blurred-face veil sprite, including seeded exceptions. An authored birth-one-star with a locked identity reveals that locked identity at two stars as an intentional clue that they are special. An ordinary generated birth-one-star reveals a custom canonical identity at three stars, with its expression variants ready or already warming. This is a viewpoint presentation rule, not a rewrite of canonical appearance or what other observers perceive.
design: Keep the generic VN renderer rules-neutral: it accepts opaque sprite handles, slots, facing, and a bounded available-expression set. The One-Star adapter projects a Master-view identity state from birth_stars, current_stars, generated_for_summon, and available approved assets. Birth-one/current-one uses a deterministic per-character assignment from a small authored masculine/feminine/neutral veil pool, never a random per-page silhouette. Seeded locked birth-one identities reveal at current_stars two; generated birth-one identities reveal at current_stars three; higher-birth-star identities retain their existing policy. Prewarm hidden assets before visible reveal: produce and hash-lock the neutral canonical sprite first, then derive face-only variants in parallel while keeping framing, body, costume, lighting, scale, and transparency fixed. Promotion must not wait for the entire sweep; a ready neutral can reveal while remaining variants finish. Start with universal neutral, happy, concerned, tense, skeptical, angry, sad, and surprised variants. Treat enraged and flirtatious, plus character-specific moods such as smug or embarrassed, as optional reviewed signature variants instead of mandatory variants for every character. Runtime LLMs see only opaque available handles and authored labels; no pixels, paths, hashes, birth provenance, or hidden reveal state.
acceptance_criteria: Master-view VN cards show stable generic blurred-face sprites for every birth-one/current-one Hero without leaking a seeded or generated identity. The same veiled Hero remains visually trackable across pages. A seeded locked birth-one Hero switches to the exact hash-bound locked neutral sprite at two stars, while an ordinary generated birth-one remains veiled until three stars and then reveals one hash-bound canonical identity. A hidden prewarm can complete across restart and cannot become player-visible before its threshold. Neutral is prioritized; missing non-neutral variants fall back to neutral without blocking the story. The eight universal expression labels select only approved variants and do not alter body, costume, framing, or background. Other viewpoints are unchanged unless their own story policy requests the veil. Tests cover both reveal thresholds, repeated/restarted pages, failed and partial prewarm, simultaneous characters, no runtime vision/path leakage, and generic non-One-Star renderer behavior.
notes: Required conflict audit: do not represent a named veiled Hero with CharacterVisuals.depiction_policy=anonymous, whose current contract forbids named visual subjects. Project an explicit stable veil identity handle for the Master viewer. Until the reveal threshold, suppress the hidden exact identity reference, reference hint, and identifying first-meeting/default-loadout face details from Master-facing narrator and image-director inputs; other viewers remain governed by their own knowledge. Establish the veil through authored story fact/context, not prompt text about renderer mechanics. Scan and reconcile existing omit/unanchored-subject, first-meeting exterior, reference-selection, and narrator visibility directions before implementation.

title: Make One-Star synthesis command survive authoritative router validation
description: Fresh session one-star-vn-background-replay-20260826 ran '/master synthesis 1 from 2, 3' with an operational level-1 Synthesis Chamber and three active Heroes. Both source agents responded, then route_authoritative_result failed loudly with 'authoritative result router output attempted to author fixed side effects'. The command returned to the prompt without a checkpoint or pending operation. A read-only status confirmed all three Heroes remained active and pending management operation was none.
design: Trace the exact fixed System synthesis plan and authoritative-result schema. Preserve adapter-owned deterministic side effects and let the router supply only the narrative/visibility fields it is authorized to judge. Reject genuine side-effect fabrication before mutation, but do not make a valid fixed command depend on the model redundantly reproducing or omitting engine-owned fields. Keep the generic authoritative-result contract shared with other adapters.
acceptance_criteria: The stored replay state plus the exact synthesis command reaches the intended pending/resolution flow without a validation false positive; source responses and guide enforcement remain routed normally; deterministic synthesis effects come only from the adapter; malformed router-authored side effects still fail before mutation. Tests cover success, rejection rollback, retry/restart, CLI/Discord parity, and confirm no Hero/pending-state mutation on failure.

title: Add a deterministic character-sprite layer to VN cards
description: The accepted visual-novel proof called for characters facing one another with small pose/expression variation, but production VisualNovelDeckSection accepts only one stage image and pages. The replay therefore showed no Iselle, Tovin, or other sprite on any reviewed-stage card. The two men visible in the opening were hallucinated inside the FLUX background, not controlled character components.
design: Extend the existing renderer with one deterministic foreground composition layer over immutable reviewed backgrounds. Use approved identity sprite variants (neutral plus bounded pose/expression choices) selected through opaque handles and authored hints. Keep identity generation/inspection in coding-time or explicit asset-review workflows; runtime LLMs never inspect pixels. Unknown/unanchored actors may be omitted without removing anchored actors or the stage. Start with a small two-character facing layout and one-character fallback rather than unconstrained scene synthesis.
acceptance_criteria: Cards can place one or two approved character sprites over an immutable reviewed stage with stable scale, facing, safe dialogue-box occlusion, and no identity/property transfer. Seeded Iselle appears when directly present; two anchored speakers can face one another; a bounded pose/expression label changes only to an approved variant; unanchored generated characters are safely omitted. The exact stage and sprite hashes are manifest-bound and load/restart/CLI/Discord paths use identical bytes. Tests cover no-sprite narration, one/two sprites, unknown actors, and privacy/reference ownership.

title: Align VN stage changes with the pages and events they depict
description: In replay turn 3, the narrator batched eight events into 20 pages. Seven events occurred in the established lobby; only final event opening_0009 moved Eren toward accommodation. Because only that final accepted director run supplied the render stage, its clear decision retroactively put all 20 pages on the neutral navy stage. Earlier event-relative director runs were cancelled as narrator_continued. One stage decision per eventual narrator batch is insufficient when the batch spans a scene transition.
design: Define one accepted-render stage contract rather than applying a last-event decision to the whole backlog. Prefer deriving stage sections only after the narrator render is accepted, using the same ordered visible-event batch. If the accepted pages span a real scene/location boundary, bind contiguous page sections to the matching before/after stages; if there is no proven boundary, preserve the prior stage. Do not expose orchestration mechanics or file paths to the narrator.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic replay of opening_0002 through opening_0009 keeps the established lobby on every page depicting the first seven lobby events and changes or clears only pages that actually depict Eren's location transition. Same-location unanchored dialogue cannot erase an established stage. Cancelled candidate runs never affect presentation. Multi-section manifests preserve ordered page/stage mapping across restart and CLI/Discord delivery; tests cover clear, replace, reuse, and a mixed-location batched render.

title: Use reviewed VN backgrounds as immutable compositor stages
description: The live replay selected the correct reviewed location handles, then destroyed their value by sending them through runtime generation. FLUX transformed the plain 1F courtyard into an ornate circular arena and hallucinated two unrelated people despite an empty-scene request. Qwen transformed the reviewed Crack plate into a generic dark corridor whose portal is two glowing grid rectangles. These failures also add 97-287 seconds of blocking latency. Reviewed canned backgrounds should be stage assets, not suggestions for a fresh background model call.
design: Keep one text-only visual-novel director contract. A replace decision chooses exactly one source: (1) stage_reference_id set to one offered exact_stage=yes reviewed environment handle with requests empty, or (2) stage_reference_id empty with one ordinary generation request when no supplied plate fits. Direct selection resolves the private frozen registry entry, atomically snapshots its exact hash-pinned provenance on the director run, bypasses every diffusion/edit job, and is revalidated before deterministic compositor cover-crop. Generated fallback retains the existing job path. Reuse walks either source through the same stage history. Runtime LLM messages contain only opaque handles, exact-stage eligibility, and authored hints, never paths, bytes, hashes, dimensions, or image analysis.
acceptance_criteria: For approved courtyard, pavilion, Crack, and Synthesis handles, a background-only VN replace selects an opaque handle, creates zero image jobs/worker calls, persists the exact reviewed source snapshot, and produces a card manifest bound to that source hash (or a documented deterministic derivative). Reuse and restart resolve the same bytes even if the currently supplied pool later changes; tampering fails closed to the neutral stage. The director may leave stage_reference_id empty and use the existing generation path when no supplied plate is appropriate. CLI and Discord continue through the shared EngineBridge deck path. Prompt/privacy tests prove LLM input contains only handles, exact-stage flags, and authored hints. A live director probe must distinguish courtyard, pavilion, Crack, Synthesis, and an unmatched scene.
notes:
2026-08-26 live image-director probe passed 5/5 without invoking image generation: ordinary 1F courtyard -> osa_loc_1f_courtyard_v1; covered arrival pavilion -> osa_loc_1f_pavilion_v1; Crack approach -> osa_loc_1f_crack_lobby_v1; Synthesis interior -> osa_loc_1f_synthesis_v1; unmatched forge -> empty stage_reference_id plus one compose request with no location guide.
Implementation committed as 95cc97f on codex/yvja-direct-approved-stages. Verification: full offline suite 1806 passed, 2 skipped; focused image/event/prompt suite 79 passed; changed-file Ruff clean; compileall app/scripts/tests clean; git diff check clean. Repository-wide Ruff is blocked only by two unrelated origin/main findings tracked in ayoa-7guw.
close_reason: Implemented and verified direct reviewed-stage selection with durable hash-pinned provenance, zero diffusion, reuse/restart integrity, shared deck composition, privacy enforcement, and explicit generated fallback.

title: Promote reviewed VN stage and identity continuity into production
description: The fresh One-Star Luna VN playtest session one-star-vn-luna-playtest-20260826 produced 7 accepted decks / 19 cards. The opening used an unreviewed dark stone lobby, then unanchored dialogue cleared the established stage for five consecutive decks. Production is not using the reviewed outdoor beginner-lobby evidence or the successful PMU reference-guided background workflow. Promote a generic authored-stage lifecycle: coding agents may inspect source images, curate exact crops, generate candidate plates, and record provenance for human review; runtime router, narrator, character-agent, rules-adapter, and image-director LLM calls must never receive or read image data. Runtime selection may use only authored text/metadata and opaque reviewed asset handles. Preserve the successful PMU outputs as tiered authored lobby plates rather than treating free-form runtime diffusion as the sole source of location continuity.
acceptance_criteria: The reference-guided background curation/generation method is codified as a discoverable repo skill with source preservation, crop/hash provenance, prompt-conflict audit, human review, and tier metadata; the skill explicitly forbids runtime LLM image reading. title: Design reusable authoritative System transition routing
description: Implement a reusable route for deterministic fictional/rules-authority outcomes that are not actor intentions. Initial use is One-Star synthesis: the command deterministically assembles affected Heroes in the Synthesis Chamber, collects source-agent last words only while the durable synthesis-resolution counter is zero, and sends an Authoritative Result plus exact fixed updates to the router for canonical facts and visibility without re-adjudicating whether the result occurs.
design: Use the existing event-router template and ClosedEventRouterOutput. A dedicated Authoritative Result user-tail envelope contains authority, fixed result, optional collected contributions, and exact fixed location/state updates. The model authors only facts and observers. Runtime rejects model-authored side effects/next-output, sets ruleset_resolution, merges fixed updates, then uses the normal prepare/broadcast/narrator boundary. An out-of-band trusted flag permits only this command path to atomically open and resolve synthesis in one transaction; it is never model-visible.
acceptance_criteria: The generic router has one minimal Authoritative Result mode with approved wording and no duplicated fidelity rules. The mode uses a closed schema, cannot open Cat II, cannot leave next_output debt, and attaches exact fixed updates rather than asking the model to re-author them. One-Star synthesis command executes teleport plus synthesis atomically; the first successful synthesis collects and preserves autonomous source contributions, later synthesis inputs omit them based on a durable adapter counter invisible to the router. Failed routing/validation leaves checkpoint, counter, character history, and ledger unchanged. Generic and D&D paths remain unchanged. Offline behavioral and rendered-input tests pass; no live harness.
notes: Implemented approved revision: router sees only the Authoritative Result mode, fictional System authority, optional collected character contributions, and exact fixed location/state updates; it has no player/binding or first-vs-later knowledge. The command drafts autonomous source utterances only while the durable synthesis-resolution counter is zero, requires the closed router result to preserve each nonempty contribution, atomically teleports guide/target/sources and opens plus resolves synthesis, clears every response frontier, and forces narration. Bound sources are never substituted by agents and no control metadata reaches the router. Pre-presentation failures leave saved state unchanged; narrator failures use the existing pending-render boundary. Verification: targeted affected suite 592 passed; full offline suite 1547 passed, 2 skipped; ruff check, py_compile, and diff check passed. No live harness, per user instruction.
close_reason: Implemented and verified the approved authoritative System-result routing and first-synthesis contribution contract.

title: Shrink the monolithic One-Star router transaction schema
description: The live one-star-human-test-adapter router exhausted max_output_tokens=8000, but retrying or merely raising the cap treats the symptom. OneStarEventRouterOutput adds a mandatory one_star_transaction union to every event, including events with no rules change. The strict provider schema is 13,227 bytes/33 definitions versus generic EventRouterOutput at 4,580 bytes/11 definitions. Its 22 added definitions contribute about 7,940 bytes: a transaction envelope, 12 unrelated operation variants, and 9 nested bookkeeping DTOs. The design also reuses durable state-shaped models such as OneStarMissionState, OneStarEquipmentEntry, OneStarSkillEntry, and OneStarPendingOperation directly in router output, while OneStarHeroDeltaOperation requires 17 fields for even a small HP or XP change.
design: First classify which values are true router judgments versus derivable bookkeeping. Keep router-owned fiction and genuinely semantic outcomes in the existing response, but project them into compact effect commands rather than full durable records. Derive catalogue effects from catalogue_id, gacha results from the adapter draw, clocks from canonical time, and unchanged Hero fields from ledger state. Avoid multiple parallel router modes unless a single compact discriminated effect surface cannot express the contract. Measure the exact strict provider schema, not the verbose Pydantic schema.
acceptance_criteria: Replace the mandatory monolithic One-Star transaction union with the smallest router-authored semantic effect contract that preserves atomic adapter bookkeeping. Ordinary fictional turns must not expose catalogue, summon, mission lifecycle, pending-operation, equipment, skill, tutorial, and feed schemas simultaneously. Durable-state models are not reused directly as router DTOs. Exact costs, timestamps, draw results, and derivable state are filled or validated by code from reviewed authority rather than restated by the router. Rendered provider-schema measurements and offline behavioral tests prove a material reduction while preserving generic narrative and D&D contracts, mission damage/progress, summons, embodied response boundaries, and atomic commit. Do not use a larger cap or automatic retry as the primary fix.
notes: Implemented one provider-facing state_updates list with one four-field OneStarStateUpdate record. Strict OpenAI schema is 5,140 bytes/12 defs versus generic 4,580/11; the old One-Star schema was 13,227/33, so 22 adapter definitions are gone from model output. Compact updates translate into private typed mutations; standard gacha derives exact draw/lifecycle internally; canonical timestamps derive from event time; unknown/duplicate detail keys fail loudly. Router context is scoped: seed static config 2,853 chars/34 lines (was 6,825/47); seed dynamic 639 chars/18 lines, and latest playtest dynamic 2,939 chars versus 5,536. Future draw slates, reserve candidates, draw counters, fingerprints, hidden capabilities, and private potential are absent. Full offline suite: 1,444 passed, 2 skipped. No live harness.
close_reason: Replaced the public One-Star operation union with one compact update definition, scoped router context, preserved atomic adapter validation, and passed the full offline suite.

acceptance_criteria: A scoped fact naming a valid but absent observer cannot disappear with only a warning. Router correction or validation either adds/repairs the required observer under an explicit safe contract or fails loudly for retry. Tests cover actor-target consequences, fully dropped private facts, confusable-id repair, and no cross-POV leakage.

title: Deliver external consequences from actor-sourced events back to the actor
description: In one-star-human-test-adapter ckpt_0003, events 036-041 were sourced from Edric's silent intentions but also canonized new goblin movement, dialogue, a spear throw, approach, and a hit. broadcast_event skips the actor's entire inbox entry, assuming an actor already knows their own action. Edric was routed next repeatedly with no Since-your-last-response facts and correctly answered that nothing had changed. Preserve suppression of redundant self-action while delivering directly observable external consequences from a mixed actor-sourced event back to that actor.
design: Use the smallest shared contract: every listed NPC observer, including the nominal actor, receives all facts visible to them. ObservableFact has no source/provenance field, so attempting to strip only self-authored clauses would require a new router schema surface or unreliable text inference. One duplicate canonical self-action is preferable to dropping authoritative external consequences; the prior assistant turn still preserves submitted intent while the inbox now carries what actually happened.
acceptance_criteria: When a canonical event contains both an actor's own action and directly observable actions or consequences from other sources, the actor receives the full visible canonical event before a subsequent character-agent turn. Self-only canonical outcomes also reach the actor so one shared observer contract replaces the unsafe actor exception. Tests cover generic self-only delivery and silence plus enemy movement, a missed attack, and a hit; existing broadcast, generic narrative, One-Star, and D&D paths continue through the shared function without adapter-specific behavior.
notes: Fixed shared broadcast contract: NPC nominal actors now receive the complete canonical event visible to them, including external responses and consequences. Also moved observation/query perception harvesting before commit/broadcast so NPC inboxes, human render buffers, and compact router history see the same final facts. Offline verification was partitioned to avoid duplicate expensive coverage: BroadcastEvent 21 passed; remaining turn-loop 106 passed; harvest+broadcast 23 passed after ordering fix; query harvest 3 passed; orchestrator+D&D bridge 25 passed. No live harness. Follow-ups: ayoa-mfmk for missing scoped recipients and ayoa-qqrr for inbox preservation across downstream failure.

title: Move One-Star gacha outcome selection into the adapter
description: The current One-Star adapter validates pool ranges, costs, identities, and atomicity, but the router still chooses each summon birth grade and reserve identity. Extend the opt-in adapter so seed-authored weighted pool odds and durable draw counters determine the actual gacha results before canonicalization, while the LLM remains responsible for fresh character identity and fictional reveal.
design: Keep the existing single router call. For each standard pool, deterministically derive the next max-batch draw preview from session identity, pool id, and a durable per-pool draw counter. Use integer seed-authored star weights; choose an eligible dormant unowned reserve of the rolled birth grade without replacement inside a batch, otherwise mark the result fresh. Project only the authoritative preview, not the hash input/counter machinery, in the volatile private router ledger. The router pairs reserve results with activate and fresh results with spawn, but may not choose or alter their grades. The reducer validates exact preview consumption, charges once, advances the counter atomically, and makes retries, reloads, and rewinds produce the same unconsumed outcomes. Opening-actor activation remains an authored non-random special pool. No pity unless separately reviewed.

title: Align player dossiers, character knowledge, and agent portrayal boundaries
description: The shared post-claim dossier contract is inverted in two ways. EngineBridge.build_character_dossier documents personality as agent-only portrayal direction but currently renders it, while it never renders player_guidance, the field authored specifically for human control. One-Star also stores author-only truths, ignorance statements, and model imperatives in private_state.secrets or known_context. The result is a 873-word Master dossier and 1,445-word Halcyon dossier containing AI portrayal prose, while the claimed Newcomer misses the System-sight and control guidance needed to play the seat.
design: Use the existing fields as one explicit audience contract, without compatibility surfaces: player_guidance is the concise human control contract and is included in the post-claim dossier; backstory and known_context contain facts the character consciously knows; private_state.secrets contains consciously known private truths; personality remains agent-only portrayal direction and is excluded from player dossiers; author-only truths remain in router hidden authority. Correct the One-Star seed to match those meanings, including Master ignorance, Iselle implementation truths, Renna hidden potential, Veil disclosure discipline, and the Warden hazard directions. Keep CLI and Discord on the same EngineBridge projection.
acceptance_criteria: The claimed Newcomer dossier contains the chosen identity and its human control and System-sight contract without fallback personality. The Master dossier excludes AI portrayal instructions, third-person novice framing, and facts defined by ignorance while retaining the interface actions and perception boundary the player needs. Halcyon receives consciously known history and private truths but no agent-only imperatives. Iselle, Renna, Veil, and Warden seed fields are reassigned or rewritten according to character awareness. Personality never renders in a player dossier; player_guidance does. CLI and Discord share the result. Offline rendered-input tests check audience placement and forbidden leakage without freezing approved prose.

title: Make One-Star synthesis and tower entry physical, interruptible transitions
description: The playtest treated synthesis and deployment as immediate Master UI effects. In the intended fiction, selected Heroes must physically travel into the Synthesis Chamber and must physically enter the gate to reach the tower. A Master selection therefore threatens movement or destruction of persistent characters and must give those characters an opportunity to respond before the irreversible transition.
design: Make selection and completion separate semantic stages. A Master action selects or summons the affected Heroes and opens or identifies the destination. Each selected Hero then receives an owed response and can walk, freeze, refuse, flee, bargain, resist, or comply. If movement is contested, normal Cat II adjudication resolves it; Iselle or the System may use only reviewed compulsion. Apply tower location changes only after physical gate entry, and apply synthesis culls and survivor mutation only after physical chamber entry and resolution. Reuse the generic contract that consequential actions against persistent characters require their intentions; keep the chamber and gate fiction in the One-Star seed or adapter.
acceptance_criteria: A Master deployment selection does not teleport a persistent Hero into the tower; a Master synthesis selection does not immediately cull or transform a persistent Hero; every selected persistent Hero receives an actionable response opportunity before crossing; willing and refusing paths both resolve without duplicate turns; multi-Hero selection waits for all required semantic responses or an explicit adjudication; location and lifecycle mutations occur atomically only after the canonical crossing; offline tests cover gate entry, chamber entry, refusal, compulsion, and multiple selected Heroes.
notes: Absorbed by staged One-Star physical operations: owner selection opens Cat II with every affected active local Hero as a required responder and makes no irreversible mutation. A later canonical crossing applies gate/chamber location and resolution atomically; refusal/cancel leaves state unchanged; deployment crossing and mission start are one event so the sealed gate cannot be bypassed.
close_reason: Deployment and synthesis are now physical, Cat-II response-gated, and atomically resolved after crossing.

title: Give Iselle lobby-wide Master-action awareness and timely tutorial turns
description: Iselle gave the Master a Synthesis Chamber overview only after the facility had already been built and used. The stored build and synthesis events observed only the Master, so Iselle had no timely fictional input. As the System tutorial guide and lobby warden, she should have near-omniscient awareness of Master-initiated management actions in the lobby.
design: Model this as an authored fictional System observation capability, never as player ownership or binding metadata. Feed Iselle relevant Master lobby actions and outcomes: summons, facility construction and upgrades, resource and store transactions, roster and loadout management, deployment selection, synthesis, promotion, and transformation. When a first-use tutorial is due, dispatch Iselle as a character agent at the correct moment; the router must not invent her dialogue. Track tutorial delivery so an overview is timely and exactly once. Keep her mission knowledge bounded to reviewed status-feed capabilities rather than granting tactical omniscience.
acceptance_criteria: Iselle receives the Master action that constructs the Synthesis Chamber before its first use; the appropriate overview can occur before the Master attempts synthesis; constructing and using the facility cannot cause a late duplicate overview; all relevant lobby management actions reach Iselle through a fictional perception channel regardless of live bindings; Iselle dialogue comes from an Iselle intention, not router-authored persistent-character action; offline tests cover observer delivery, first-use ordering, and duplicate suppression.
notes: The adapter now enforces Iselle guide observation for Master lobby-management mutations and records actually observed tutorial deliveries exactly once. Keep this bead open for the remaining character-turn timing/playtest question: code does not force Iselle dialogue or deterministically require a tutorial before first facility use; her agent and router still own whether and when she speaks.

title: Author exact One-Star premium summon pools and single-source synthesis rules
description: The latest playtest exposed two unsupported mechanics. A failed synthesis claimed that multiple source Heroes were required, then Iselle invented the same rule; a later synthesis invented a maximum of three sources. A premium five-pull also produced birth-grade one-star Heroes. These outputs conflict with the intended fiction: one real source Hero is sufficient for synthesis, and premium summons must not produce Heroes born at one star.
design: Put exact domain authority in the One-Star story or its modular rules adapter, not in generic router machinery. Basic summons may draw fodder-grade birth-one-star Heroes. Premium summons start at birth two-star unless a future reviewed rule explicitly changes the pool. Synthesis accepts one or more real source Heroes, so one source is valid; do not invent a minimum above one or an unreviewed maximum. Keep star-at-birth distinct from current star rank. Give the router compact authoritative facts and give state mutation a matching validation contract so prose and persistence cannot disagree.
acceptance_criteria: A premium summon cannot canonically create or activate a birth-one-star Hero; a basic summon still can; a synthesis with one valid source Hero proceeds to the normal embodied response and resolution flow; no prompt or adapter asserts that multiple sources are required; no unreviewed source maximum is invented; birth-star and current-star fields remain distinct; offline tests cover basic versus premium pools and one-source versus multi-source synthesis; the existing atomic summon and synthesis lifecycle issue is linked.
notes: Absorbed by the One-Star adapter: seed-authored basic and premium birth-star ranges are enforced; birth and current stars remain separate; synthesis accepts one or more real sources with no invented maximum; offline tests cover one-source, multi-source, and invalid pool cases.
close_reason: Seed-authored summon pools and source-unbounded synthesis are now enforced by the adapter.

title: Enforce per-fact perceptual channels across locations and mediated views
description: The Floor-1 return event marked corridor disappearance facts all_observers while also listing lobby-only Petra, Tam, and Iselle, giving them remote detail they could not witness. Later the Master was explicitly left on a management view and excluded from Renna's arrival, then was included in Rowan's next hall scan without any canonical feed switch. Iselle was routed to announce mission status without receiving the Master-only terminal result and guessed 'Floor 2 cleared' after a failure. Event-wide observers and story-mediated POV state are not sufficient to keep each fact on its actual fictional channel.
design: Make visibility a per-fact fictional perception contract. Multi-location transitions must explicitly target the characters and channels able to perceive each side; all_observers must not bridge locations. Model durable mediated capabilities and state such as the One-Star Master's selected live feed and Iselle's authorized System-status channel as fictional context, never as player or binding metadata. Router output should be rejected or corrected when facts claim observers without an established perceptual path.
acceptance_criteria: A gate/teleport event delivers corridor facts only to floor witnesses and arrival facts only to lobby witnesses, while the Master receives only the active feed plus private UI. Switching between management and hall/floor views requires a canonical state change and observer inclusion remains stable until then. Iselle either receives a participant-safe terminal status through her authored System channel before being routed to report it or is not routed as an authority. Offline tests cover multi-location facts, mediated view switches, guide status, ordinary shared rooms, and binding invariance.
notes: The adapter now persists Master active-feed state and enforces Iselle-mediated lobby-management delivery. Keep this bead open: generic per-fact multi-location visibility and mediated-channel enforcement remain broader router work beyond the adapter ledger.

title: Sanitize narrator control bytes without flattening prose
description: The final accepted narrator output contains eight C0 control bytes, U+0019, U+001C, and U+001D, in place of apostrophes and quotation marks, and CLI prints them unchanged. Separately, player-output privacy redaction uses whitespace splitting and joining, collapsing multi-paragraph narration into one paragraph. Both interfaces therefore receive text that differs materially from the accepted narrative form.
design: Create one shared final-text boundary for CLI and Discord. Normalize the known truncated-punctuation controls, reject any remaining forbidden C0 bytes before persistence and delivery, and apply privacy redaction without destroying authored newlines or paragraph structure. Persist and deliver the same validated text so checkpoint replay cannot resurrect unsafe bytes or a different layout.
acceptance_criteria: Narrator final_text with known punctuation controls is normalized deterministically; unknown forbidden controls fail loudly before history, receipts, checkpoint, or delivery commits. Privacy redaction removes protected content while preserving line and paragraph breaks. CLI and Discord receive byte-equivalent validated prose. Offline tests cover the stored corrupted sample, multiline narration, redaction across line boundaries, rollback, and checkpoint reload.

title: Reject router-authored actions for persistent characters without intentions
description: On two Master defer turns the router directly puppeted Iselle: it authored her welcome speech and later made her announce the Synthesis Chamber. No Iselle agent intention existed. The later announcement also regressed chronology by calling a chamber newly opened after it had already been built, viewed, and used. Current prompt prose says defer should route an existing named character as next output, but runtime accepted the violation.
design: Make the ownership contract source-neutral: canonical facts may not invent deliberate speech or action for a persistent CharacterRecord unless that character supplied an intention in the current adjudication packet. A router continuation may author environmental or System pressure and actions by explicitly router-owned minor opposition; it must select a persistent character as next_output rather than speaking for them. Cat II resolution may combine the submitted participant intentions it actually received.
acceptance_criteria: A defer/continuation result that puts new dialogue or deliberate action in an existing character's mouth without a submitted intention is rejected before broadcast/persistence and retried or routed to that character. System-only cues and nameless minor opposition remain router-authorable. Regressions cover both Iselle incidents, an environmental continuation, a normal submitted agent action, and Cat II resolution without adding controller knowledge to the router.

comments.author: dan
comments.text: The late Iselle Synthesis Chamber tutorial is another persistent-character puppeting case. See ayoa-k3xp.

title: Preserve source order for same-offset narrator facts
description: Narrator projection sorts facts by at_offset_s, duration_s, then source_index. In two accepted kills this moved a shorter System defeat notice ahead of the same-offset physical outcome: one goblin was announced defeated before its gurgle, slump, and still fact, and another lost HP before Davan drew and delivered the killing thrust. The canonical source sequence was correct; the narrator received it reordered.
design: Treat the router-authored fact sequence as the causal tie-breaker. Sort visible facts by effective offset and original source index, not duration, unless the schema later gains an explicit independent sequence field. This is a narrow regression follow-up to completed lossless-compression work ayoa-ipi3.
acceptance_criteria: The two stored same-offset fixtures render input in canonical causal order, including physical outcome before its derived System notice. Facts at different offsets remain chronological, stable source order is preserved for ties, and no prose wording is frozen. Targeted offline tests cover same-offset unequal durations and multi-event POV batching.

title: Expose same-beat spawn identities to the first narrator render
description: The opening narrator rendered Niflheim First Summon 01, 02, and 03 because run_beat composed prose before the orchestrator applied the generated Davan, Petra, and Tam CharacterRecords. First-introduction tracking also marked only Iselle. The router's spawn fact also flattened all three into rusted-blade fighters even though its own seeds requested a swordsman, staff-wielder, and knife-fighter and the generated records carried distinct equipment. Existing fixes expose spawned identities to immediate agent dispatch and later router turns, but not to narration or fact-safe identity projection for the spawning event.
design: Keep the spawn event canonical facts limited to details guaranteed by the authored spawn request; reject or retry facts that contradict explicit role and loadout seeds, and do not invent one generic appearance for heterogeneous spawns. Await the already-shared spawn-authoring result once before composing any render that contains that spawn. Build a shallow speculative roster for narrator, name, and visual projection, then reuse the exact same records for accepted post-beat application. Keep persistence transactional: narrator continue, failed rendering, or rollback must not commit roster records or introduction ledgers, and accepted narration must not generate or apply a character twice.
acceptance_criteria: A spawn event's canonical facts do not contradict its explicit role or loadout seeds, and its first player-facing render uses every generated display name and public visual identity instead of raw ids or a false shared loadout. Introductions commit only after the render is accepted, and identical records are reused for immediate agent dispatch, image direction, later router context, and checkpoint state. Continue or failure paths leave no committed characters or introductions. Offline tests cover heterogeneous multi-spawn openings, immediate responders, narrator continue and rollback, and idempotent post-beat application.

title: Preserve authored identity across dormant activation
description: In event 63 the router activated seeded reserves without their authored public identity/loadout. It turned Rowan, a two-star knife scout with mismatched knives, into a bow-and-blade fighter and Renna, a bow skirmisher with an ash shortbow, into a swordswoman with a rusted blade. The active-only initial roster excludes dormant reserves, and compact prior_event history serializes spawn, dormant, and cull but omits activate, so runtime knows more precise lifecycle truth than the router.
design: Project only the exact public identity and loadout needed for an eligible authored activation candidate at the activation turn, after the cached system prefix and without exposing private material or binding state. Record each accepted activate id-to-location transition in compact router history. The exact CharacterRecord should outrank broad story defaults; clarify Renna's authored bow as an exception to the general one-star starter-blade rule. Preserve the blank player-authored Newcomer contract: an unclaimed blank slot stays dormant, absent from agent/router play, and is never treated as an activation candidate.
acceptance_criteria: A dormant authored reserve's first canonical appearance, narrator render, and first agent observation agree with its display name, role, appearance, and exact loadout. Compact router history retains the activation id/location without replaying the full roster. Rendered-prompt tests show volatile candidate data only in the user tail and no controller/binding leakage. Renna keeps her bow, Rowan keeps his knives, the unclaimed Newcomer remains invisible and undispatched, and non-One-Star activation behavior remains rules-neutral.
notes: The adapter preserves exact Hero mechanics and lifecycle for dormant reserve activation and exposes eligible IDs/birth stars to the router. Keep this bead open: the transition-specific router projection still needs the exact dormant reserve public identity/loadout contract described here rather than relying on activation history afterward.

title: Audit latest One-Star playtest end to end

Treat router-authored canonical facts as truth and separate invention from rendering. Inspect exact stored model messages and rationale, not just final prose. Do not run live models or mutate the session.
acceptance_criteria: A severity-ranked, deduplicated finding set covers the entire playtest from ckpt_0000 through ckpt_0024, cites stored evidence and current source cause, labels fixed-versus-current status, identifies downstream effects, and creates one scoped Bead per current actionable defect. No source files are changed during the audit.

comments.author: dan
comments.text:
Completed end-to-end read-only audit of all 25 checkpoints in one-star-human-test-death through ckpt_0024. Scope included 81 canonical events, 21 CharacterRecords, nine character conversations, 23 narrator renders, visibility logs, compact router history, current prompt/schema/runtime sources, logs, and the image job database. Three independent agents audited router/canonical flow, character/world behavior, and narrator/image/player delivery. No source/session/test files were changed and no live models, harnesses, or services were run.

Top current defects:
1. P0 ayoa-9kna: five summons produced only two records; three phantom Heroes were then consumed with no culls or target mechanics while named selected sources received explicit plot armor.
2. P1 ayoa-n8jq: dormant activation lacked authored identity/loadout and activate was absent from compact history; Rowan and Renna swapped weapon concepts.
3. P1 ayoa-sdwi: same-beat spawn identities were unavailable to the first narration, exposing raw ids and contradictory generic loadouts.
4. P1 ayoa-xvpg: router puppeted Iselle twice on defer without an Iselle intention and announced an already-used chamber as newly opened.
5. P1 ayoa-6o82: narrator sorted same-offset facts by duration and rendered two System defeat notices before their causal kills.
6. P1 ayoa-fx6w: accepted final_text contained eight C0 controls and output privacy processing flattened paragraph structure.

title: Make One-Star Tower floors non-retreatable without extraordinary escape
description: One-Star seed guidance currently permits mission failure by being forced to retreat, but the intended world is harsher: once deployed onto a Tower floor, ordinary retreat or return to the lobby is impossible. Escape requires an established very rare item or sufficiently powerful magic. Update the story-authored router/agent guidance and remove contradictory retreat assumptions without adding generic-engine or D&D machinery.
design: Encode this as One-Star story truth in the seed, not generic runtime logic. Distinguish tactical withdrawal within a floor from escaping the floor itself. Deployment commits the party until the floor is cleared, the party is incapacitated/killed, or an already-established extraordinary escape method succeeds. Do not invent a convenient escape item or spell merely because the party wants to leave.
acceptance_criteria: The shipped One-Star seed explicitly states that ordinary retreat from a Tower floor to the lobby is impossible after deployment; only an established very rare item or sufficiently powerful magic can permit escape. Tactical repositioning within the floor remains possible. Existing mission/failure guidance no longer treats ordinary forced retreat as an available outcome. Seed validation and focused offline behavioral/contract tests pass.
close_reason: Updated the One-Star seed so deployment seals ordinary lobby return, tactical withdrawal stays within a floor, and escape requires an already-established very rare item or very powerful magic. Propagated the contract to router/narrator world context, generated and seeded character knowledge, guide/Master guidance, and status adjudication while preserving the blank Newcomer and inert Warden. Added offline semantic contract coverage; full suite: 1288 passed, 2 skipped.

title: Make forced narrator handoffs render-only at safety caps
description: When max_agent_cascades_per_beat or max_events_per_beat forces delivery, run_beat passes handoff_policy=forced but does not expose the cap as narrator context. NarratorFinalOutput still permits handoff=continue with empty final_text, and the forced path ignores that value and commits the text, so a model contract violation can produce a blank accepted render even though it cannot restart the cascade. Tighten the generic forced-handoff contract without teaching the narrator engine cap machinery.
design: Keep cascade and event caps as engine-only safety controls. Forced narrator calls should have no actionable continue choice: require a non-empty render and preserve unresolved visible action as unresolved. Soft narrator candidates retain render-or-continue. Prefer a unified schema/runtime invariant or a genuinely closed forced-output schema over prompt-only wording; reject violations before clearing buffers or committing history.
acceptance_criteria: At cascade_cap and max_events_cap, the narrator receives a semantic forced-delivery contract and cannot cause or return an accepted continue. Empty final_text or handoff=continue fails loudly before buffers, history, visual introductions, or image transactions commit. Soft handoff candidates can still return continue and resume through the router. Offline tests cover both caps, a forced-contract violation, and the unchanged soft candidate path; no engine cap terminology leaks into final_text or model-visible implementation prose.

title: Prevent targetless router continuation from crashing a turn
description: Live One-Star session one-star-human-test-death failed at 2026-08-20 18:51:30. A normal router result returned event_kind=beat_continues with no dispatchable next_output, correctly invoking Continuation Required. The continuation response repeated event_kind=beat_continues with no next_output; ClosedEventRouterOutput admits that shape, so run_beat hit its deliberate second-rescue RuntimeError. This is a generic continuation-contract gap, not a One-Star seed or image-worker failure.
design: Make beat_continues imply an actual semantic frontier everywhere: at least one observer must have routing_role=next_output. Remove prompt guidance that uses targetless beat_continues as an engine continuation sentinel. When a scene needs motion but no character should act yet, the router must author the grounded environmental/opposition change in the current canonical event and classify that real surface (usually state_change, public_fact, response_requested, or ambient_pause). Retain route_continuation only for an explicit narrator continue handoff; do not use it to repair malformed router output. Backstop the prompt with EventRouterOutput validation and preserve a loud error for an unusable selected target.
acceptance_criteria: A Continuation Required response cannot reach run_beat as event_kind=beat_continues without a dispatchable next_output. Preserve the loud invariant and router-owned canonical truth: do not silently close, relabel, or summarize an inconsistent event. Keep one generic rules-neutral continuation contract, avoid a retry loop, and do not add D&D-specific machinery. Add offline coverage for rendered mode instructions, response validation, successful closed cues, successful routed continuations, and the observed repeated-targetless shape. Verify the saved checkpoint remains retry-safe; use at most one cache-friendly live replay if live validation is requested.
notes: Implemented a unified generic invariant: event_router.txt now makes targetless beat_continues invalid and requires an observer with routing_role=next_output. Mission-stall guidance now authors concrete pressure in the current canonical event instead of using a targetless continuation sentinel. EventRouterOutput validation rejects the invalid shape, and run_beat retains a pre-broadcast loud guard for mutated or non-validated outputs. The old missing-target continuation rescue was removed; route_continuation remains only for explicit narrator continue handoff. Updated stale Cat II fixtures to use cat_ii_open. Verification: consolidated affected suite 312 passed; full offline suite 1287 passed, 2 skipped; git diff --check clean. Per user direction, no live harness was run. Existing session process was not touched and must be restarted to load this code.
close_reason: Targetless beat_continues is now forbidden by the router prompt and schema, with a loud pre-broadcast runtime backstop; offline suite is green.

description: One-Star playtests consistently preserve every Hero and produce compliant one-star lobby recruits, contradicting the setting's intended brutality. Initial/random one-star Heroes have diverse, durable conflicting survival drives and at least some can refuse deployment, freeze, flee, hoard, bargain, sabotage, or provoke lobby consequences. Keep this bead open: brutality, refusal diversity, and ordinary-play lethality remain story prompting and playtest concerns, not deterministic adapter policy.

title: Make Cat II actor submissions origin-agnostic
description: A character's contestable action currently can open Cat II when submitted by a human but is forced through ClosedEventRouterOutput after a character-agent call. Unify actor-submission adjudication so identical fiction has identical Cat II semantics regardless of its communication source.
design: Treat character-agent public_text as a proposed actor submission until the router canonicalizes it, not as already-committed motion. Use one semantic submitted_actor_id plus submission_text contract and Cat-II-capable response path for human and agent actor submissions. Keep genuinely router-authored continuation/repair modes closed. Coordinate the agent-submission wording in event_router.txt with the prompt/seed sibling issue.

title: Make narrator compression semantically lossless
description: The narrator already receives an ordered per-POV batch of canonical visible facts, but current dramatic-economy and response-shape wording permits omission, missing buffered events are skipped, and accepted empty prose can flush a whole batch. Preserve every distinct visible fact while allowing fluent clause-level compression.
design: Adopt a lossless semantic compression contract: compress syntax, not events; preserve every distinct fact in order and protect exact dialogue, gesture/signal content, source/target, contrast, refusal/consent, state changes, tactical preparation, attempts/outcomes, and causal/temporal order. Remove hard prose caps that conflict with fidelity. Fail loudly on missing buffered events or an accepted render with empty final_text. Do not add coverage ids, a parallel schema, or a second model pass.

title: Make event routing binding-neutral end to end
description: Remove live-control and interface knowledge from every constructed event-router message and make next_output semantic for every character. Unify fresh character submissions regardless of human or agent origin; remove binding-derived Player Characters and NPC roster splits, binding engine updates, control-dependent story seed rules, and D&D control fields/filters. Keep live binding resolution exclusively in the downstream dispatcher and preserve absent player-authored slots through semantic dormant/not-yet-fictional state.
design: Use one active-character roster with fictional identity, status, location, objectives, and perceptual capabilities. Use explicit submitted_actor_id plus submission text for all in-fiction inputs. For begin/arrive, provide opening_participant_ids or arriving_character_id as semantic directive inputs; do not provide active_viewpoint_ids if it is binding-derived. Router observer selection must follow perception only. D&D reaction/loot/roll choices must be semantic character opportunities, with interactive versus automatic resolution downstream. Treat cascade/event caps as runtime safety boundaries and persist or explicitly resolve any unserved next_output frontier.

Identical human/agent submissions use the same adjudication schema and can open Cat II. next_output ids are identical across bindings and all Cat II/runtime consumers resolve them through one binding-aware path. No binding/control/interface terms or derived roster membership enter shipped router prompts or story context. D&D planning packets omit player_controlled/player_roll_mode. Cap tests prove bounded execution and no silent loss of response debt. Targeted offline tests, full pytest, and live generic/D&D router harnesses pass.

title: Keep narrator handoff reasons diagnostic-only

title: Audit constructed router prompt for binding neutrality
description: Crawl every production contributor to the fully constructed event-router message array across fresh actions, agent outputs, continuation, Cat II, begin/defer/query/time/scene modes, compact history, schemas, and rules adapters. Determine whether fictional routing and response pressure are independent of live human bindings, interfaces, and agent-vs-player dispatch. Audit the autonomous cascade cap as the runtime safety knob. This is an evidence-only audit; do not edit source.
acceptance_criteria: Record exact rendered evidence and file/line locations for all modes; distinguish necessary character/POV semantics from live-control leakage; give a severity-ordered verdict, recommendations, and tests; explicitly confirm or reject that the whole constructed prompt is user-agnostic today.
notes:
VERDICT: FAIL. The full constructed event-router request is not user/control/binding agnostic.

Rendered production evidence: Spring Rain fresh call produced roles system,user. System said every character currently bound to a human and included the story fact that named characters may be claimed and unclaimed characters are AI-driven. User tail included Acting Character plus a binding-derived Player Characters list, then Initial Roster labeled every active NPC. Agent output produced system,assistant,user with a clean current tail such as pip: Pip nods once and compact prior_event history, but reused the same control-aware system. Continuation produced the full Player Characters tail plus no autonomous actor language. DND Cat II produced system,user and its packet contained player_controlled true on participants plus player_roll_mode prompt.

P1 prompt leaks: app/prompts/event_router.txt:2-8 defines NPC output and player delivery; 38 distinguishes committed agent output and forbids Cat II; 97 and 158 alter observer inclusion for human-bound characters; 126-136 alter departure and feasibility by player versus NPC/agent origin; 162-176 and 186-209 use NPC-only response/pacing; 268-276 make begin, arrive, defer, query, and time directives player/binding aware; 339 manually describes observer ids as NPC or human-bound; 402-409 injects Player Characters. Correct neutral text at 180 is contradicted throughout.

P1 constructed context leaks: app/engine/context_builder.py:568-620 builds only CURRENTLY-BOUND characters and documents that membership means human, never agent. app/engine/turn_loop_dispatcher.py:137-211 excludes collect_player_ids from Initial Roster, so binding changes derived membership even without labels; 760-795 injects the binding block on fresh, continuation, and generic Cat II calls. The unbound player-authored blank exclusion at context_builder.py:517-527 is valid only as semantic dormant/not-yet-fictional status. turn_loop_dispatcher.py:222-257 injects pending engine mutations; engine_bridge.py:1864-1869, 2014-2027, 2131-2149, 2237-2253, and 2397-2422 emit human, AI control, player-bound, protagonist, narrator POV, and agent-resume text. These updates are transient rather than their own compact history records, but may steer canonical output that persists.

P1 origin-dependent adjudication: fresh route uses EventRouterOutput and may open Cat II, while route_agent_output at turn_loop_dispatcher.py:1212-1279 uses ClosedEventRouterOutput. event_router.txt:38 hard-codes this and event_router.py:654-665 structurally forbids agent-authored Cat II. Identical fictional attempts can therefore resolve differently based on whether runtime called an agent. The bound/unbound formatter branch at dispatcher.py:935-944 currently renders identical raw text, but remains a derived control branch.

P1 next_output violations: generic normal routing correctly resolves semantic ids downstream at turn_loop.py:2744-2765. Cat II bypasses it. turn_loop.py:1055-1064 filters resolution followups directly to agents; the human-responder close path uses it at 2917-2925, and the all-agent inline close path at 3276-3290 ignores explicit resolved next_output and falls back to the initiator. DND adds binding filters: dnd_cat_ii.py:4016-4047 drops human social targets, and 4050-4106 defines stealth followup through player versus non-player rolls.

P1 DND leaks: event_router_ruleset_dnd5e.txt:35-59, 87-107, 132-170, and 172-207 distinguish player action, player-facing reactions, NPC continuation, and player-only loot. dnd_cat_ii_router.txt:65-68 distinguishes player-controlled stealth. dnd_cat_ii.py:3130-3192 puts player_controlled and player_roll_mode into the model packet even though 1216-1274 already resolves actor control and interactive rolling downstream.

P1/P2 story context leaks: router world lore includes raw facts/lore via dispatcher.py:121-134. Spring Rain seed line 50 says claimed human versus AI-driven. One Star seed lines 63-67, 109-115, and opening line 150 make perception, death safety, activation, and summon branches depend on human binding. Replace these with durable character capabilities/status and semantic opening participant ids.

Already neutral: event_router_ruleset_default.txt; the content-lookup preflight template by shape; strict generated JSON schemas for EventRouterOutput, ClosedEventRouterOutput, and DndEventRouterOutput had zero player/human/bound/binding/NPC/agent/control/frontend/interface/user terms; compact prior_event projection at dispatcher.py:509-662 carries canonical facts, observer roles, pacing, and next ids without controller metadata. Manual schema prose is not neutral, and ClosedEventRouterOutput remains semantically origin-dependent. The normal downstream binding resolver is the right seam.

Replacement contract: one unified active-character roster independent of bindings; explicit submitted_actor_id and submission text for all sources; opening_participant_ids and arriving_character_id only for author directives; fictional status/location/perceptual capabilities for visibility. Do not use active_viewpoint_ids if derived from bindings because that is the same leak under a neutral name. Runtime alone maps next_output to yield versus agent. DND reaction, loot, and roll opportunities identify semantic character ids; runtime chooses interactive versus automatic handling.

Caps: defaults are 35 agent handoff attempts and 40 canonical events per beat at turn_loop.py:2592-2640 and state.py:631-641; background threads cap at 4. Cap paths force narrator composition, flush human buffers, release slots, and prevent unbounded compute. They are not lossless: max-events checks before binding resolution at turn_loop.py:2800-2810; an agent cap on an earlier ordered target can preempt a later human target; cap termination stores no executable pending frontier. Compact history can retain next=id, but the owed response is not automatically resumed. Narration covers accumulated canonical facts and can be locally coherent, but an unresolved autonomous response may be abandoned. Persist the frontier or explicitly define/canonicalize cap cancellation.

Tests required: exact rendered-array invariance under binding permutations for every audited mode; one submission contract/schema for human and agent paths with Cat II allowed; next_output binding matrix proving identical router output and downstream yield/agent behavior including Cat II; unified roster and opening participant tests; negative prompt hygiene across shipped story seeds and engine updates; DND packet and followup invariance; cap tests for ordered mixed targets, max-events precedence, and durable unresolved debt; then full offline tests and live generic plus DND router harnesses. Focused audit checks passed: 4 tests, 174 deselected. Followup implementation bead: ayoa-vp4x.
close_reason: Completed exhaustive constructed-message, schema, adapter, history, and cascade-cap audit. Verdict is a definitive failure of binding neutrality; evidence and replacement contract recorded, with implementation followup ayoa-vp4x.

title: Repair render retry, image cancellation, and ordered handoff regressions
description: Review of commit bb1836d found five coupled runtime regressions in the binding-aware render path: canceled transactions can leave succeeded director runs selected forever; a continuation followed by narrator failure can persist stale retry metadata; an empty first NPC response can suppress later ordered targets; a multi-POV failure can anchor retry to the wrong POV event; and closed-event image work completed during retry can be labeled as the next turn. This bug fixes only findings 1-5 and references ayoa-rqr4 and ayoa-bwlf; narrator/router ownership and router prompt wording are intentionally out of scope.
design: Preserve the existing rules-neutral render contract and canonical event buffers. Prefer explicit per-attempt retry snapshots and persisted turn provenance over compatibility paths or duplicate runtime channels. Do not change narrator handoff_reason or event-router prompt behavior in this issue.
acceptance_criteria: Transaction cancellation excludes every associated director candidate, including already-succeeded rows, from status selection and a regression proves no permanent render wait. Durable narrator failure state is rebuilt from the actual failed attempt after any continuation and retains all accumulated event/runtime effects. Ordered dispatch skips silent exhausted NPCs and reaches later targets. Pending retry uses the selected gate POV's event anchor. Replayed closed-event runtime uses the failed turn's persisted source turn index for image lineage. Focused regressions and the full offline pytest suite pass; scoped changes are committed and pushed.
notes: Implemented five scoped fixes. Transaction cancellation now cancels succeeded director candidates and render-status queries exclude all cancelled transactions. Pending narrator state is rebuilt per render attempt and anchors to the selected gate POV. Silent NPC output advances to the next ordered target. Durable retries create closed-event runtime with the already-persisted turn index. Added five regressions, including accumulated dormant side effects and real checkpoint image lineage. Verification: 202 focused tests passed; full suite 1271 passed, 2 skipped; git diff --check passed.
close_reason: Implemented and fully verified all five post-commit runtime regressions.

title: Move player-handoff decisions to the binding-aware dispatcher
description: The router intentionally reasons about in-world actors and observations rather than frontend users, live bindings, or who is waiting behind a seat. That abstraction becomes incorrect when the router is also expected to decide when a beat should be shipped to a player. In one-star-human-test it called non-playable Dara a player-controlled Hero, ended autonomous mission beats for the player controlling Dara, and repeatedly returned tactical affordances to a Master who could only watch. Preserve the router abstraction: it should report semantic pacing and actor pressure, not infer user identity or frontend delivery. The turn-loop/dispatcher already owns live character bindings and must combine router output with that authoritative information to decide whether to continue autonomous dispatch, request a human-bound character action, render an observer update, or terminate a beat for a genuine story reason. Related symptom bead: ayoa-yghp.
acceptance_criteria: Router input/output carries story semantics and requested actor participation without frontend/provider identity or a parallel user-awareness schema. Every routed event uses one ordered binding-aware target contract: the first bound human yields for player input, the first dispatchable NPC continues autonomously, and unbound player-authored seats retain the existing loud rejection. When no target remains, a player-visible batch is a narrator handoff candidate; the narrator may request continuation only for established motion or a submitted wait condition, while Cat II, query, rules, harvest, and safety-cap boundaries force rendering. Candidate prose/history/images are discarded on continue, the full buffer reaches the eventual accepted render, and provider-failure retry does not replay the player action. Tests cover NPC and human response targets, ordered mixed targets, multiple private POV batches, absent authored slots, defer/watch, no target, caps, and shared CLI/Discord contracts. Live generic and D&D router harnesses plus a One-Star Master-only replay validate the flow.
notes: Implemented the binding-aware target resolver and narrator render/continue gate without a second mission schema or adapter side channel. The live generic router harness after prompt tightening routed both fresh and repeated defer to Dante rather than back to Dan; raw report: app/storage/playtest_reports/router_prompt_targeted_20260820T020156Z.json.
close_reason: Implemented and verified binding-aware handoff, narrator continuation, durable retry, and closed non-Cat-II continuation behavior in offline and live One-Star runs.

title: Let the router author nameless minor enemies and make utility agents cheap
