title: Trigger image direction at player-render boundaries
description: The current image sidecar runs once for every visible canonical router event. In one-star-human-test, 82 routed events produced 82 image-director calls and 124 requested images even though narration rendered only once per player-facing beat; no image jobs or deliveries were created because the presentation/generation path was unavailable. Move image selection to the player-render boundary: after autonomous routing and agent cascades have produced the bounded event batch that will be narrated to a player POV, start one image-director query concurrently with that narrator render. Immediately before invoking the image director, check that the target frontend/POV has a usable image presentation path and that generation can accept work. If not, bypass the director entirely. This is related to ayoa-ke4k, but concerns invocation ownership and suppression rather than delivery progress UX.
acceptance_criteria: A player-facing render causes at most one image-director call for its complete visible canonical event batch, launched concurrently with narrator composition rather than once per router event. Intermediate autonomous cascades never invoke direction independently. No director call occurs when no eligible player render exists, the target POV/frontend cannot present an image, or generation preflight cannot accept work. CLI and Discord use one shared POV-safe presentation capability contract. A narrator continue decision cancels speculative image work and retains the full render buffer; accepted prose and image work commit together after checkpoint persistence. Player-facing prose waits until the accepted render's director makes no request or every requested image reaches success/failure; there is no arbitrary short race deadline. Tests cover long cascades, display-capable and prose-only targets, unavailable generation, private POV batches, narrator veto, and commit/rollback. A live One-Star replay shows bounded illustration cadence.
notes:
Supersedes the original nonblocking-prose criterion after design review: local diffusion is free, so accepted player prose should wait for terminal image work rather than racing a 20-second tandem deadline.
Render-bound image transactions are now speculative across the full per-POV buffer, canceled on narrator continue, and committed only after checkpoint persistence. Direction is skipped before invocation when worker preflight or frontend presentation is unavailable; admitted-request finalization prevents indefinite prose waits after queue rejection. Shadow mode and the 20-second tandem race were retired.

title: Fallback: add One-Star state adapter only if router history fails
description:
Preserve exact One-Star mission, tutorial, resource, reward, and post-clear continuity, but treat a story-specific state adapter as the last resort rather than the starting design.

First attempt the smaller router-owned contract. At floor initialization, the router explicitly declares the immutable completion and failure conditions plus current progress (for example, "defeat all enemies; 0/5 defeated"). Every routed mission event keeps the latest concise mission status in router context through the existing compact canonical-history path, independent of what is rendered to Heroes. Untimed missions also let the router author concrete, motif-consistent pressure when a beat makes no objective progress; timed missions rely on their objective clock. Pressure may not change the declared completion target or decide Hero actions.

Do not add One-Star fields to generic narrative schemas. Do not implement a content-state adapter merely because checkpoints lack structured One-Star mechanics. Escalate to the smallest story-specific, rules-neutral adapter only if targeted live runs demonstrate that router-owned history cannot maintain exact objectives, timers, resources, or atomic transitions without contradiction or drift.
design:
Preferred first pass:
- Use the existing router output and compact prior_event history rather than a parallel mission-state store.
- Put the exact mission declaration in non-observable router diagnostic/context material, not canonical_event.observable_facts, so Hero knowledge remains independent.
- Retain only the concise mission-relevant router declaration needed for continuity; do not restore raw user messages or broad rationale boilerplate.
- The router updates the latest status after outcomes it authors. Never infer progress from narrator prose, generated character records, or cull signals.
- Freeze the completion/failure contract when the floor begins. Untimed pressure can worsen circumstances, reveal or reposition established threats, and advance motif consequences, but cannot silently change a fixed denominator.
- A timed objective still needs one internally consistent remaining-time declaration; do not add a second generic pressure mechanic.

Adapter escalation threshold:
Use a One-Star-specific adapter only after repeatable blind-play evidence shows stale counts, contradictory clocks/resources, invalid spends, or failed clear/return transitions despite the compact-history contract. If escalation is necessary, persist only the mechanics that require computation or atomic validation and feed their current projection to the router.
acceptance_criteria:
Before any adapter implementation, exercise the router-history approach in targeted offline and blind live runs. The router must carry exact completion/failure conditions and current progress across mission beats without leaking hidden status to Heroes; fixed objective targets must not drift; untimed non-progress must produce motif-consistent pressure; timed missions must retain a coherent clock.

Document any repeatable contradiction or loss of state that justifies escalation. If no such failure is found, leave the generic engine and One-Star content_state schema unchanged.

If an adapter becomes necessary, keep it story-specific and rules-neutral; persist only demonstrated computational state; make spends/rewards atomic; provide player-safe CLI and Discord projections; cover deployment cost, rewards, damage/equipment wear, clear/return, checkpoints, and non-One-Star isolation with offline tests.
notes: Adapter escalation is complete under the approved 2026-08-21 contract. The opt-in One-Star adapter is authoritative only for reviewed bookkeeping, exact references, atomicity, clocks, and persistence; router/agents still own fictional judgment, damage, death, growth, consent, and resistance. It covers configured economy/facilities/research, summons, Hero state, missions, staged deployment/synthesis/promotion, guide tutorial ledger, status/image projections, transaction repair/rollback, and checkpoint reload. Final offline result: 1410 passed, 2 skipped. No live harness was run per explicit user instruction. Intentional boundaries: no arbitrary currency delta; equipment provenance remains router-owned; dynamic rival-Hero mechanics are future scope if needed.
close_reason: Approved lightweight One-Star adapter is implemented and passes the full offline suite.

title: Apply combat-start feature and spell declarations mechanically

Root concern: dnd_combat_start can canonicalize/narrate player feature or spell declarations without routing them through adapter-owned resource/effect application, so the fiction says a spell/feature is active while combat state does not.
acceptance_criteria: When a player declares class features or spells as part of combat-start escalation, the D&D adapter either applies legal immediate resources/effects before hostile resolution, queues/asks for a legal turn-order decision, or refuses to narrate the mechanical effect. Regression should cover Hexblade's Curse plus Armor of Agathys at combat start: resource spend, temporary HP/active effect, and later damage behavior are coherent, or the narration explicitly withholds those effects until a legal action occurs.
notes: Deferred design option from 2026-05-26 discussion: if more proactive combat-start routing does not solve combat-start declarations, consider a typed opening-turn rule where the initiating player resolves one declared action at the top of initiative and forfeits their normal turn for that first round. Do not implement this unless prompt/router preemption remains insufficient.

title: Design router long-context management without upstream compaction
description: Long campaigns must remain under repo-owned context management. We do not want to rely on provider/upstream compaction for the event router. Scope and implement a router context strategy that preserves the router's actual runtime contract while bounding tokens: deterministic prior_event history windows, durable campaign/beat state projections, selected content-packet retention and expiry, visibility/privacy-safe summaries where needed, and instrumentation that reports router input budget by section. The design should account for imported module content packets and normal rules-neutral stories.
acceptance_criteria: Router calls never depend on upstream/provider compaction to fit context; router input construction has explicit local budget policy and section-level token diagnostics; long-session tests or harnesses verify relevant events, unresolved beats, visibility constraints, and selected content packets survive while stale detail is dropped or summarized; implementation preserves the rules-neutral narrative engine and keeps D&D/imported-content machinery modular.

title: Scope content-manager catalog input before large modules
description: The Lost Laboratory cgf prompt review showed the content-manager input sends a first-N global router_lookup_catalog slice plus every seeded knowledge-map entity. In the 2026-05-25 Kwalish demo, the content-manager prompt was 47k-49k chars / 11.8k-12.2k prompt tokens; available_catalog alone was 34.7k chars / ~8.7k tokens for 120 rows. Lost Laboratory has only 133 catalog rows, so the cap mostly hid the problem. About 80/120 rows in the route-scene catalog were dormant/future material by a simple active-character/location heuristic. For a Strahd-sized module, the same first-N-by-ref projection will either omit relevant active-region refs or spend a large prompt on unrelated actors/locations. Replace this with an import-authored scoped catalog/projection policy: include current location neighborhood, active fronts, candidate character refs, recently mentioned/known refs, and explicit startup seed requirements; do not dump the whole catalog or all dormant entity rows into each content-manager call.
design: Corrected framing: this is not primarily a new prose chunk hierarchy. The goal is token-minimized router knowledge dispatch. A content card remains the reviewed runtime record/full packet that code can fetch and validate. The content manager should usually see only a tiny import-authored dispatch index: stable knowledge keys with minimal labels/summaries, scope facets, activation/trigger hints, and counts/pointers to full router packets. Primary mode: from recent canonical facts, active location/fronts, candidate characters, and known router knowledge keys, decide which router knowledge keys must be expanded before the next router call. Engine code validates selected keys and expands them into full reviewed router content records. Agent-side broadcasts/knowledge-graph updates are rare edge-case catches only; imported character agents should start with the context they need, and thereafter learn from router-authored observed facts. The full knowledge graph is not the normal payload to the content manager; it exists to catch missing router knowledge or unusual state transitions. Lost Laboratory migration should prove that prompt size scales with active semantic scope, not total module card count, and Strahd should be tested with a synthetic large index before importing the full module.
close_reason: Implemented key-based content-manager dispatch index, validated router packet expansion, and verified Lost Laboratory startup CLI demo with scoped prompt input.

title: Define module application profiles for checkpoint seeds and existing stories
description: D&D modules should be modular imported content packs, not story checkpoints. Define the durable contract where a reviewed module can either generate a new seed checkpoint or apply an authored projection/application profile to an existing checkpoint. The design must distinguish content pack authority, projection profiles, seed creation, and bounded additive checkpoint application.
acceptance_criteria: A design/implementation contract exists for content packs, projection/application profiles, seed generation, and additive checkpoint application; Lost Laboratory-style projection artifacts are aligned with that contract; obsolete import/demo surfaces that imply bespoke module-to-checkpoint assembly are removed or updated; follow-up implementation beads exist for any runtime application APIs not completed in the cleanup.
notes: Cleanup pass completed on 2026-05-24: DND_MODULE_IMPORT now describes the current content-pack/projection/application contract; superseded lookup/living-enemy draft docs and stale story_importer review report were removed; the manual module vertical-slice test now builds through ContentPackProjectionArtifact and content_pack_state_from_projection instead of hand-assembling legacy imported-content state. Remaining work under this tracker: first-class named module application profiles, existing-checkpoint apply API, seed/checkpoint validators, conflict validation, and pack locator resolution.

title: Constrain imported-module NPC spawns to reviewed authority
description: Lost Laboratory deep CLI demo report app/storage/playtest_reports/lost_laboratory_cli_demo_20260524T193810Z/report.md shows the Cartophile introducing and spawning Meris Venn as a required custodian even though the reviewed startup catalog already has named candidate actors/companions. For imported-module play, router/agent convenience spawn paths need a reviewed authority check or explicit generic-NPC policy so module agents do not replace cataloged choices with unreviewed named NPCs. Add tests around imported-content scenes where an NPC proposes a companion/custodian: reviewed actor refs may be used, but new named durable NPCs require explicit spawn authority or a generic bystander role.
close_reason: Closed as already resolved by the later imported-module context fix: this was not a generic NPC spawn-authority bug, but a failure to provide the router enough reviewed/imported context to choose from existing catalog actors. The underlying context delivery has been fixed elsewhere.

title: Require valid D&D stats before spawned NPCs join combat
description: Lost Laboratory deep CLI demo report app/storage/playtest_reports/lost_laboratory_cli_demo_20260524T193810Z/report.md reached route/combat, but final combat state included spawned story characters as active D&D combatants with 0/0 HP, notably npc_bandit_captain and npc_meris. In D&D terms, an NPC that can participate in combat should have HP; the bug is that generic/story spawn paths promoted narrative characters into active combat records without reviewed stat authority or an explicit default/generic stat profile. Fix the narrative-character to D&D-combatant bridge so a character can join active combat only after the adapter attaches reviewed mechanics, applies an approved default/generic stat profile, or fails loudly before inserting the combatant. Truly non-participating bystanders can stay outside active combat, but they must not appear as active 0/0 HP combatants.
acceptance_criteria: Combat start with existing generic spawned NPCs or companion/bystander characters never produces active 0/0 HP combatants. Regression covers imported-content combat where spawned story characters are either given reviewed/default D&D mechanics before joining, left outside active combat as bystanders, or rejected with a loud validation error. The fix preserves D&D mechanics inside the adapter and does not add rules assumptions to the generic narrative engine.
notes: Reopened after design correction: D&D-session narrative NPC generation should ask the character_gen LLM for bounded D&D stats, with the default profile retained only as a defensive fallback for old or malformed characters.
close_reason: Completed: D&D-session narrative character generation now uses a D&D-specific response schema and prompt extension so the same character_gen LLM emits a bounded statblock. The adapter converts authored statblocks into character mechanics with source=character_gen_dnd_statblock; generic non-D&D spawns keep the old schema and receive no D&D prompt/schema text; the default profile remains only as an old-save/malformed-output backstop.

title: Remove content-pack refs and hashes from character-agent prompts
description: Lost Laboratory soak 20260524T144931Z character-agent prompts included pack ids, agent_context refs, and sha256 hashes inside in-world character identity text. These did not echo into player prose, but they are implementation/source-tracking metadata and should not be part of character-agent natural context unless there is a specific reviewed reason.
acceptance_criteria: Rendered character-agent prompts for imported content do not expose pack ids, content refs, or sha256 hashes in in-world identity/current-state text. Add a negative rendered-prompt hygiene test for imported-content agent prompts.
close_reason: Completed: rendered character-agent imported-content context now redacts pack ids, content refs, and hashes; added negative prompt hygiene coverage and verified Lost Lab prompt rendering plus targeted pytest/ruff.

title: Fix player-facing D&D damage roll display

This is distinct from duplicate damage application: even valid damage records should render trustworthy dice/formula output and current HP/status when relevant.
acceptance_criteria: Player-facing CLI combat output never renders damage as d20 ? = 0 for non-d20 damage. Damage lines show the actual damage formula/result or a clean total-only fallback, and combat summaries expose enough HP/status context to maintain trust.
close_reason: Completed: D&D damage-only rolls now render damage formula/total and target HP/status without d20 ? output in CLI/Discord projections; targeted display/combat tests passed.

title: Load required module content before resolving scout exploration
description: Lost Laboratory soak 20260524T144931Z let Gearbox enter the cave and report interior details while the demo was intended to have the whole imported module available. Treat this as a content pipeline/import/playtest setup failure, not a character-agent responsibility: Gearbox should not know or reason about what is reviewed startup content. The engine/content-manager/router should have the authoritative module slice needed for current exploration, or should pause, lookup, and load before resolving concrete interior facts. Secondary UX symptom: player formation later placed Gearbox in the middle while runtime state had Gearbox already inside the passage.
acceptance_criteria: Manual Lost Laboratory demo initializes/imports enough module content for the exploration area being played, or content-manager performs an engine-side lookup before router/agents resolve new area facts. Character-agent prompts do not mention reviewed-slice/import availability. Regression covers Gearbox-like scouting into a newly reached area: if content is available, facts come from the content packet; if content is unavailable, the engine/router does not ask a character agent to invent the area.
close_reason: Closed per user as already resolved by later imported-module context and private seed coverage fixes; these no longer represent separate remaining work.

title: Prevent friendly opportunity attacks in D&D combat resolution
description: Lost Laboratory soak report 20260524T052726Z reached 30 turns, but the combat transcript shows an invented friendly-fire reaction: after pc_expedition_leader defeated the panther, Gearbox moved/withdrew and the combat manager produced a Demo Expedition Leader longsword attack against Gearbox for 3 slashing damage. No player requested attacking Gearbox, and no hostile trigger justified an ally-opportunity attack. Investigate combat-manager action/reaction targeting and add regression coverage for allied movement after a hostile is defeated.
acceptance_criteria: A D&D combat-manager regression fixture with an allied NPC moving or withdrawing after a hostile drops must not create a player attack against that ally unless the player explicitly declared a hostile reaction; player-facing transcript must not show invented friendly-fire rolls.
close_reason: Completed: non-current actor combat actions now allow only legal readied releases or enemy opportunity attacks. Regression coverage rejects same-faction friendly opportunity attacks and preserves hostile-spawn opportunity attacks against party NPCs. Lost Laboratory soak 20260524T144931Z observed Gearbox movement without a friendly opportunity attack.

title: Auto-end D&D combat when spawned hostiles are defeated
description: Extended Lost Laboratory soak playtest 20260524T050239Z showed active_combat stayed open after mon_panther_1 reached 0 HP/defeated. Automated NPC turns continued through the combat manager with no live hostile threat, burning calls and leaving exploration blocked unless a human manually runs /combat end. Add deterministic combat-end detection or an explicit router/combat contract for when all hostile spawned combatants are defeated, preserving manual override for unusual encounters.
acceptance_criteria: A combat where all hostile spawned combatants are defeated exits active initiative or produces a clear player-facing manual-end prompt without continuing automated NPC combat turns; regression coverage uses a D&D combat checkpoint with a defeated monster and active allies.
close_reason: Completed: spawned hostile defeat now auto-ends D&D combat. Regression coverage exercises a combat-spawned hostile reduced to 0 HP and confirms active_combat clears. Lost Laboratory soak 20260524T144931Z observed 'All hostile combat-spawned monsters are defeated; initiative ends automatically' with manual_combat_end_used=false.

title: Run extended Lost Laboratory CLI soak playtest
description: Continue the throttled Lost Laboratory field CLI playtest for roughly 30-40 turns so we have longer-run evidence of content-manager cadence, combat/exploration behavior, checkpoint stability, and player-facing transcript quality after the initial field/combat pass.

title: Throttle content-manager preflight calls
description: Live Lost Laboratory CLI playtests show route turns call the content manager before every router pass. Since LLM latency dominates, add a conservative throttle so the content manager runs only every few route cycles, while still forcing a call when pending content signals need draining or no router content has been introduced yet. Continue the Lost Laboratory playtest and inspect content-manager/router call logs after the change.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime route/continuation/agent-output paths skip content-manager calls on throttled cycles without losing pending content signals; tests cover the throttle, forced pending-signal behavior, and router-only packet projection; a Lost Laboratory CLI report shows fewer content-manager calls during exploration/combat and records the content-manager audit.
notes: Implemented with deterministic pending-content drain on skipped cycles rather than forcing a content-manager LLM call; this preserves reviewed router packets while avoiding the latency hit.
close_reason: Implemented content-manager refresh throttling, preserved deterministic pending-content drain on skipped cycles, validated with tests and Lost Laboratory field playtest report app/storage/playtest_reports/lost_laboratory_cli_demo_20260524T042357Z/report.md.

title: Tighten imported-module startup handoff pacing
description: Lost Laboratory deep CLI playtests can reach the startup negotiation, accept Cartophile terms, appoint Garret as map custodian, add Gearbox as technical support, and ask to depart, but the router keeps cascading NPC acknowledgements instead of closing the handoff and time-skipping to the route. This blocks a full start-to-field imported-content playtest without a manual field-start checkpoint.
acceptance_criteria: A live or harnessed Lost Laboratory deep scenario can complete the startup handoff, leave the Cartophile scene, and reach the Barrier Peaks route after terms/roles are accepted; router still gives NPCs turns when a new material decision or objection exists; tests or report assertions cover that dormant/off-stage NPCs are not spawned just because content-manager hints mention them.

title: Promote Lost Laboratory field encounters and statblocks

To playtest module-faithful combat, promote reviewed encounter/statblock/tactical-map or theater-of-mind slices from the OCR review into runtime-ready content.

title: Continue Lost Laboratory CLI exploration/combat playtest

title: Demo Lost Laboratory content manager in CLI

title: Wire content manager packet into router preflight
description: Wire the prototype content_manager into the imported-content loop with the corrected split: content_manager input may include recent canonical facts plus the compact engine-owned knowledge map; output should update the engine-owned knowledge map, identify router turn candidates, identify router-required content refs/packets, and optionally flag agent context broadcasts for rare non-router knowledge changes. The event router must receive only the projected candidates plus newly required router knowledge alongside its ordinary input/history, not the whole knowledge map.
acceptance_criteria: Content manager schema distinguishes engine knowledge-map updates from router projection fields; engine validates and applies knowledge updates deterministically; router preflight projects only turn candidates and required content packets into router context; optional agent broadcasts validate character ids and reviewed refs; tests prove the router prompt does not receive the full knowledge map.

title: Simplify content manager router packet

title: Prototype content manager LLM role

The role should use GPT-5 mini via a dedicated OPEN_AI_CONTENT_MANAGER credential and produce structured proposed content updates from compact recent canonical facts plus compressed entity knowledge context. Keep code validation responsible for applying or rejecting refs; do not give the router raw graph authority.
acceptance_criteria: LLM config recognizes a content_manager role backed by GPT-5 mini and OPEN_AI_CONTENT_MANAGER; missing-credential reporting includes the new env var; a prompt/schema/helper exists for content-manager proposals from recent facts and entity knowledge; tests cover role config, prompt/schema output shape, missing refs/invalid update validation, and no private source/path leakage.

title: Emit import-time semantic projections from reviewed catalog
description: Use the reviewed semantic catalog as the import-time source of truth for runtime projections. During manual or automated import, the authoring/promote step must decide semantic slice boundaries and projection membership: character initial prompt details, initial knowledge graph, router startup context, router lookup catalog/index, engine overlay inputs, and checkpoint seed inputs. The runtime engine should load and validate those prepared projections; it should not rediscover character slices, initial router context, or knowledge-graph split points every session.
acceptance_criteria: Importer/promoter emits durable projection artifacts from the domain catalog for router startup context, router lookup/index packets, character-agent initial context, initial knowledge graph, engine overlay inputs, and checkpoint seed inputs; projection artifacts preserve refs/hashes back to reviewed catalog records and fail loudly on missing, blocked, unreviewed, or stale refs; Lost Laboratory demo/seed path consumes the reusable projection artifacts instead of bespoke script-level actor/context/graph slicing; tests cover missing refs, blocked/unreviewed records, compact packet shape, initial knowledge-map construction, character prompt privacy, router startup context, and no private paths/source text in runtime/public outputs.
notes: Implemented generic import-time content projection schema/builder plus Lost Lab CLI demo consumption. Local private Lost Lab promoter now emits semantic_projections_full_reviewed_v1.json with 133 router lookup entries, 15 character projections, 15 knowledge-map entities, and private engine overlay metadata. Runtime startup/field seeds now load prepared projection packets instead of recomputing actor/context/graph slices from the raw catalog; router lookup catalog prefers projection metadata and omits hashes from prompt blocks. Tests added for missing refs, blocked/unreviewed records, compact router catalog packets, initial knowledge map, character prompt privacy, startup/field seed loading, and public metadata sanitization.

title: Review and promote smaller-module semantic catalog slice
description: Review the first private OCR/manual semantic catalog pass for the smaller module and turn a bounded vertical slice into approved runtime authority. Split or merge draft records by logical play boundaries, fill missing actor context slices and graph edges, and choose the startup/checkpoint slice deliberately rather than relying on page boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: A reviewed import report identifies the chosen vertical slice, approved runtime-ready records exist for startup locations, principal actors, active fronts, lookup packets, agent slices, and checkpoint seed inputs, compiler output has no blockers for that slice, and no raw source text, protected excerpts, source paths, or private extraction artifacts are committed.

Runtime smoke verified lookup/catalog records contain no private paths, raw text markers, or source-file markers. Out of scope remains downstream keyed areas, maps/images, statblocks, combat automation, and later-site actor turns.

title: Remodel knowledge structure and import smaller module slice
description: Define the ideal knowledge structure for imported modules that balances agent-driven story, router turn orchestration, engine-owned non-decision state, and knowledge-graph lookup. Then follow the manual PDF import guide against a smaller local module PDF, producing private extraction/import artifacts and documenting blockers if the source is unavailable or unsuitable.
acceptance_criteria: Design docs/schema plan capture the target knowledge structure; the smaller module PDF is inspected/extracted if present; a first manual import artifact or documented blocker exists; follow-up Beads are filed for remaining implementation passes; no raw PDF text, private source paths, protected excerpts, or private extraction artifacts are committed or exposed.

Follow-ups filed as ayoa-ae2 for review/promotion and ayoa-40v for runtime projections. Existing ayoa-cgf and ayoa-16g cover lookup delivery and live harness work.
close_reason: Implemented the schema/design pass, produced private first-pass OCR and semantic import artifacts for the smaller local module, verified targeted tests, and filed follow-up work for review/promotion plus runtime projections.

title: Expand living enemy design with module examples
description: Update the existing semantic catalog/living enemy design note with the user's refined responsibility split and sanitized concrete example patterns from the private module OCR. Do not create a new design file; do not quote or expose raw module text, source paths, protected excerpts, or private module title.
acceptance_criteria: Existing design note is updated in place, captures router turn-orchestration authority, engine ownership of non-decisions, character-agent story-driving context, likely knowledge graph/lookup role, and includes sanitized module-derived examples that inform the design tradeoffs without leaking protected source content.
close_reason: Updated existing living-enemy design note with refined router/engine/agent responsibility split, knowledge-graph direction, and sanitized module-derived example patterns.

title: Document semantic catalog living enemy design

acceptance_criteria: Markdown file exists in the repo, explains the catalog/checkpoint/agent-slice plan, explicitly calls out the two-model concern, and frames the living-enemy design as an open review decision rather than a settled implementation.
close_reason: Completed tracked draft design note for semantic catalog and living enemy review.

title: Redesign imported-content lookup catalog delivery
description: Redesign how imported-content references reach the router now that page-proxy measurement catalogs are retired. Decide and implement the smallest durable contract for module lookup: main-router typed ref requests with non-LLM validation and compact packets, a separate bounded lookup/content-manager LLM, deterministic retrieval, or a hybrid. Keep reviewed authority checks in code; do not let any model invent refs outside the advertised/compiled catalog. Token budgets should be based on the semantic catalog/current compiled lookup shape, not page-proxy heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: Current separate preflight and main-router flow are either unified or explicitly justified with measured token budgets from semantic/runtime catalog artifacts; runtime code validates pack/ref/hash/runtime-ready status before any router knowledge packet; the router receives compact knowledge packets only after validation; tests cover hallucinated refs, unapproved/flagged records, catalog cap behavior, and prompt/runtime privacy hygiene; documentation or Beads notes capture the chosen loop and when a separate LLM is warranted.
notes:
Design boundary from 2026-05-24: lookup/catalog delivery should consume import-time projection artifacts. The content-manager/router lookup loop may choose which validated packet is needed now, but it should not split raw module semantics into character/router/engine slices at runtime.
Demo cleanup on 2026-05-25: added a dedicated Lost Laboratory --scenario cgf that exercises projection/catalog delivery without entering the long combat soak; report now records per-role usage totals and compact content-manager prompt budgets instead of dumping full prompt rows; content-manager prompt projection strips pack-ref hashes while validation still fills hashes in code. Live cgf run app/storage/playtest_reports/lost_laboratory_cli_demo_20260525T042300Z passed 17/17 checks. Measured content-manager calls: 2; catalog refs per call: 120; hash-like prompt tokens: 0; full input tokens: 11805 and 12209. Remaining cgf design issue: the separate content-manager prompt is still roughly 12k input tokens per run against the full Lost Laboratory projection catalog, so the bead remains open for catalog/knowledge-map slimming or a stronger justification of the separate LLM loop.
close_reason: Completed: dedicated Lost Laboratory cgf demo now passes with measured projection/catalog budgets; 12k-ish content-manager input is accepted as expected for the separate content-manager loop over the full projection catalog, with hashes stripped from prompt refs and code-side validation preserved.

title: Measure full private module catalog token cost
description: Compile a local private measurement pack from existing private module extraction artifacts and calculate the token cost of router reference catalogs at full-module scale. The artifact is for architecture measurement, not reviewed runtime authority; do not expose raw module text in Beads, git, logs, or final user output.
notes: Compiled private measurement pack private_module_full_ocr_measurement with 258 unreviewed flagged page-proxy cards and 615 aliases. Runtime card loading returns 0 cards; include_flagged reader returns 258. Token report private_module_full_ocr_catalog_token_report.json records aggregate costs only: current full 258-card lookup shape 14,706 tokens, current default 80-card cap 4,560 tokens, minimal ref/kind/title 6,966 tokens, minimal plus aliases 10,320 tokens, derived-title index 9,557 tokens, compact packet all cards 19,203 tokens, naive full OCR body total 235,414 tokens. Artifact is measurement-only, not runtime authority.

title: Expand private-module seed coverage for mist-road escalation
description: Haiku-agent CLI playtest of the private-module seed reached /story start, /join, /begin, the first content lookup, and a D&D contested social roll, then failed loudly on the next player action because NPC-introduced mist-road details referenced reviewed content that is not present in the local runtime pack. Add reviewed/paraphrased runtime cards for the mist hazard, watcher pressure, sound/lingering encounter trigger, and near-term shelter destination, or revise the local seed so NPCs do not introduce those details before reviewed authority exists. Keep refs/aliases sanitized; no source paths, OCR text, protected excerpts, source labels, or private source titles in Beads/Git/player output.

close_reason: Closed per user as already resolved by later imported-module context and private seed coverage fixes; these no longer represent separate remaining work.

title: Add Discord AI-agent playtest harness
description: Scope and implement a Discord-level playtest harness where AI agents act as synthetic players against the real Discord frontend, instead of bypassing Discord through EngineBridge or CLI. The harness should exercise slash-command flow, session/channel mapping, POV thread or DM delivery, roll prompts, asset reveal delivery, retries, and cleanup. Avoid user-token self-bot automation; use a test-guild-safe adapter or approved bot/test-account workflow.
design: Prefer a small Discord driver layer with pluggable actor policies: scripted actions first, LLM-generated player agents later. Keep assertions at the frontend contract: what each synthetic user could see and what the shared channel saw, not internal checkpoint state unless diagnosing a failure.
acceptance_criteria: A single command can launch or connect to a test bot in a test guild, create/resume a throwaway session, bind two or more synthetic players, feed agent-generated actions through the same Discord command/delivery path a human uses, capture main-channel/thread/DM outputs, assert no private output falls back publicly, and clean up test messages/session refs. The harness writes sanitized reports and never stores Discord tokens, private source labels, or protected module text.
close_reason: Out of scope per product decision: Discord playtesting will stay human/manual; maintain CLI parity instead of building AI-agent Discord automation.

title: Add imported-content live playtest harness
description: Current coverage proves the content pipeline through offline synthetic tests, but there is no repeatable live/manual harness that bootstraps a private compiled pack, starts a module-backed session, drives representative player actions, captures the lookup/router/narrator calls, and emits a sanitized report. Add a harness so future imported-content playtests do not depend on ad hoc CLI driving or private state inspection.
acceptance_criteria: The harness can run against a local private compiled pack and a sanitized seed; it records raw model-call metadata and sanitized outputs under ignored playtest reports; it checks lookup preflight insertion, one-time router content memory, missing-content loud failures, D&D Cat II/combat content context, front signals, safe asset reveal payloads, and privacy leakage; it preflights required provider credentials before the first live call.
notes: Additional manual CLI evidence: Haiku-agent private-module run reached story start, join, opening render, imported content lookup, and a D&D contested social roll with router/narrator/combat-manager on defaults. title: Define router prompt contract for content history records
description: Review of commit 63e6164 found content_known, location_card, and front_signal records are appended as assistant-side router history, but the event router prompt does not define these record types or the meaning of visibility=hidden/scope=router. Without an explicit contract the router can treat hidden module data as ordinary prior assistant context and launder summaries, hazards, clues, front knowledge, or pressure into observable facts.

notes: Constraint from design review: fix this with the smallest router-visible contract that works. Do not dramatically increase the number of terms, fields, schema surfaces, or prompt modes. Reuse the existing compact content record shapes (content_known/location_card/front_signal), existing observable_facts visibility rules, and existing generic router structure as much as possible. Prefer clarifying semantics for the current modular records over adding parallel content-specific machinery.

acceptance_criteria: A test with an otherwise pristine checkpoint plus pending content signals verifies the first router call includes the initial roster block and also includes content records only in router history. Opening non-content stories remain unchanged.

Dodge is a universal 5e combat action and should not require D&D Beyond to list it as a sheet action. title: Surface missing D&D combat manager API key cleanly
description: CLI playtest session cli_takeover_haiku_20260520 hit an internal error when a combat turn first invoked dnd_combat_manager. Router and narrator had role keys, but dnd_combat_manager had no OpenAI key; verbose repro logged: openai.OpenAIError: The api_key client option must be set either by passing api_key to the client or by setting the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable. Acceptance: combat setup or first combat action detects missing dnd_combat_manager credentials with a clear CLI-facing configuration error, or role-key fallback/config docs make this impossible in normal local playtests.
notes:
Reopened after review: router-key fallback is incorrect because all role keys should be loaded from the same shell environment. Remove fallback and fix exact role env loading instead.
Follow-up correction: do not load role keys from ~/.bashrc at runtime. Keep the explicit combat-manager key contract and put OPEN_AI_COMBAT_MANAGER in the local gitignored .env instead.

title: Continue a sparse VN opening through its owed autonomous guide
description: The fresh Master opening delivered two sparse cards ('Pale summon-light...' and a System registration notice) and returned control even though opening_0001 already owed Iselle's autonomous welcome and the Master had no meaningful response. The player had to issue /defer before any embodied scene or dialogue appeared. The tuned handoff cadence then correctly continued autonomous responses, so the initial forced begin boundary bypasses the useful ownership-aware judgment.
design: Keep /begin as the explicit start action, but use the same semantic handoff ownership contract for its first beat. When the opening leaves only an autonomous response owed and no meaningful player response available, continue into that response before first delivery. Preserve a bounded safety cap and render immediately if the opening itself creates a real player choice.

An opening that genuinely asks an embodied player or Master for a choice stops immediately. title: Tune VN narrator page rhythm and direct-address readability
description: The live Luna VN playtest exposed a narrator-authored broken page boundary in deck 67d594c282c80f35a467e69c44d056d3ed5fe8b80c403bb4d78a23a0999b5d88: page 1 ends mid-sentence with 'her knife stays tight in her' and page 2 is only 'other hand.' The raw narrator conversation already contains that split, so this is not compositor wrapping. In event_0004, the agent said 'I can’t offer you another way out ... but you may inspect'; router canonicalization stored bracketed character ids, and the narrator rendered 'Mara Pell' twice, producing safe but robotic direct address. Do not attribute Iselle's 'Acknowledged!' phrasing to the narrator: it originates in the character-agent output.
acceptance_criteria: Every VN page is a semantically complete beat and never continues an unfinished sentence solely to satisfy a preferred character limit; long facts are compressed or kept on one readable page; unambiguous spoken second-person address stays natural without leaking source ids or changing target/meaning; dialogue/action order and handoff boundaries remain intact; tests exercise rendered messages/schema/correction behavior rather than freezing prompt prose, and a targeted live replay covers a long action sentence plus bracketed direct address.
notes:
Decision 1 (2026-08-26): remove the narrator prompt's numeric page-character target. Require pages to end at complete semantic boundaries. Also change deterministic compositor pagination so overflow moves at sentence/utterance boundaries instead of cutting every four wrapped lines. Collect remaining prompt decisions before implementation.
Decision 2 (2026-08-26): choose natural direct-address option A. In quoted speech, bracketed labels are referent anchors rather than necessarily literal names; preserve the referent while restoring natural grammar, use second person for the addressee, and avoid repeated full-name expansion. Before edits, scan the entire rendered VN narrator input, shared partials, correction path, and compositor contract for conflicting directions.
Decision 3 (2026-08-26): choose ownership-aware option A. Reuse the handoff-condition block to expose whether a player-owned response is currently available and whether an autonomous responder is queued. Keep narrator judgment, but bias handoff cadence using recent /defer frequency separately from historical substantive player involvement: frequent defers favor batching; a history of active participation favors preserving earlier response opportunities. Replace conflicting frequent-interruption/routine-answer rules rather than appending exceptions.
Implementation (2026-08-26): removed the VN character-count target and conflicting routine-answer/frequent-interruption rules; both narrator modes now use one ownership-aware cadence contract. Candidate handoff context carries bounded per-POV counts (last 6 submissions for defer frequency, last 24 prior submissions for substantive involvement), current meaningful player-response availability, autonomous-next availability, and existing commitments without replaying prior player prose. The compositor v5 joins likely adjacent mid-sentence same-channel fragments, preserves unpunctuated short utterances, paginates ordinary overflow at sentence boundaries, and uses measured clause/line fallback only for a physically oversized sentence. Prompt-only direct-address attempts failed live, so the root canonical contract now preserves spoken pronouns with silent identity anchors (for example, you [character_id]); narrator projection strips roster-owned anchors deterministically while agent observations retain safe identity anchors. Final live report app/storage/playtest_reports/vn_narrator_tuning_20260826T203448Z passed router producer, direct address, long sentence/card fit, privacy, and repeated-defer spectator continuation checks. Full suite: 1797 passed, 2 skipped.
Regression evidence (2026-08-26): checkpoint ckpt_0003 event opening_0006 stores three pronoun anchors. replace_character_ids_for_narrator strips 'you [ids]' and 'your [ids]' but not contraction 'you’re [ids]' because the regex requires whitespace immediately after the pronoun. Deck 58249cf5cc31bf79434f284d37893e1f77b9f3d999ecf86a6356de15c8e08685 page 12 renders 'once you’re [Marta Vell,Tovin Rusk,Eren Vale]'. Extend the deterministic contract to apostrophe contractions without weakening source-id rejection; add grouped roster-anchor and curly/ASCII apostrophe regressions.

title: Validate persisted One-Star derived Hero sheets
description: Deterministic progression owns Hero stats and hp_max, but checkpoint validation currently accepts a structurally valid persisted sheet without recomputing it from progression_seed, birth/current stars, potential grade, affinities, and level. An altered sheet can therefore survive unrelated later events and evade replay verification. Also tighten potential_grade >= birth_stars and progression configuration lower bounds needed for strict three-stat affinity allocation.
design: Reuse rebalance_hero on a deep copy as the source of truth; do not add another stat formula or expose private progression inputs to any model.
acceptance_criteria: A shared validation helper recomputes the deterministic sheet at load or transaction boundaries while preserving current HP deficit, rejects mismatched stats/hp_max, requires potential grade not below birth grade, and rejects progression configs incapable of allocating the configured strict affinities. Current One-Star seed, synthesis, generic narrative, and D&D offline tests remain valid.

title: Deterministic One-Star Hero generation and progression
description: Replace model-authored numeric One-Star Hero sheets with adapter-owned deterministic generation and progression. Character generation supplies only qualitative strong/weak stat affinities plus equipment, skills, and characterization. The adapter owns replay-stable birth stats/HP, hidden growth potential, XP awards and level-up growth, cap banking, promotion carryover, and seeded-Hero rebalancing. Keep private potential out of all router, narrator, character-agent, and Master surfaces; preserve generic and D&D behavior.
design: Use seed-configured fixed-point formulas: level-1 means by birth grade, deterministic +/-5 percent totals, strong-stat-high/weak-stat-low distribution, potential-grade stat and HP growth, cumulative XP threshold 50*L*(L-1), per-floor survivor XP with overlevel multipliers, cap bank limited to one extra level. Remove router authority over level, XP, stats, and HP max. No old-checkpoint compatibility shim.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh generated One-Star Heroes always receive replay-stable nonempty stats and HP without numeric model output; hidden potential is durable and never projected; Renna uses grade-4 potential while Newcomer remains ordinary; seeded Heroes are rebalanced and existing levels receive threshold XP; mission completion deterministically awards and applies XP/growth/cap banking; promotion applies banked XP; router-authored numeric progression is rejected; One-Star-only offline tests pass and generic/D&D behavior remains unchanged.
notes:
Root cause confirmed 2026-08-23. This is not stat erasure and not merely weak prompt adherence. Every fresh generated One-Star Hero found across adapter sessions (14/14 across adapter-2 through adapter-5) was born with stats={}; seeded reserves retained populated stats. character_gen_ruleset_one_star already asks for a few legible stats. AuthoredOneStarHeroMechanics models stats as dict[str,int]. Anthropic SDK structured-output transform removes additionalProperties from all object schemas and sets additionalProperties=false; therefore the effective Sonnet schema for stats is type=object, properties={}, additionalProperties=false, making {} the only legal value. hidden_capabilities has the same defect. Local Pydantic and adapter validation accept empty maps, so the forced empty object persists unchanged. Correct implementation direction: use a model-facing list of fixed-shape stat entries (stat_id/value), convert to the durable dict after parse, require at least one entry, and assess hidden_capabilities similarly; do not hardcode story stat names. Existing checkpoint records were generated empty and were never later cleared.
Implemented deterministic fixed-point birth stats/HP, strong/weak affinity allocation, private potential-grade growth, XP thresholds/floor awards/overlevel scaling, cap banking/promotion carryover, seeded-Hero rebalance, and replay validation of derived sheets. Numeric chargen and router progression authority retired. Offline verification: full suite 1524 passed, 2 skipped; Ruff/compile/diff checks clean; no live harness.
close_reason: Deterministic generation/progression contract implemented and fully verified offline.

title: Prioritize dialogue in narrator compression

title: Preserve character inbox when post-agent routing fails
description: CharacterAgent commits a successful agent draft by clearing pending_observations before the router adjudicates that new intention. If downstream routing or event preparation then fails, the character's incoming facts may be durably consumed even though no canonical response event closes. Audit transaction ownership and ensure retry/recovery preserves the inbox or the committed user turn without duplicating action.
acceptance_criteria: A character-agent response followed by router, adapter-prepare, or persistence failure cannot lose the observations that produced it. Retry/recovery has one coherent conversation/inbox state, no duplicated agent action, and no silent fact loss. Tests cover router exception, adapter validation/repair failure, and successful normal drain.

title: Represent persistent non-social hazards without character-agent interiority
description: The seeded Warden of the Eighth is a persistent CharacterRecord whose personality says it is not social and should have no dialogue or human interiority, while known_context says it should never be given intentions. The universal character-agent contract requires every AGENT-TURN to end in a private intention, and persistent-character ownership rules prohibit the router from inventing its deliberate action. Once activated, the Warden therefore has no coherent owner. The same gap applies to named recurring mechanisms, traps, constructs, and environmental hazards outside D&D.
design: Add one rules-neutral ownership representation for persistent non-social scene entities. They need stable identity, appearance, location, state, tells, and canonical continuity, but no character-agent goals, secrets, dialogue, or private-intent turn. Router or an optional rules adapter may adjudicate their authored behavior under explicit capabilities without creating a second social-character path. Re-evaluate whether this belongs as a typed scene entity rather than a CharacterRecord; retire any obsolete fields or readers instead of adding a compatibility shim. Keep D&D hazards modular and relate the boundary to router-owned minor opposition.
acceptance_criteria: The Warden can persist, be perceived, expose readable attack patterns, act, take damage, and be defeated without a character-agent prompt or fabricated private intention. title: Collapse duplicated One-Star authority in router construction
description: The rendered One-Star begin router system message is 107,697 characters before the volatile user tail. design: Inventory every semantic rule and assign exactly one authoritative seed surface for each audience. Project a compact omniscient router view from that source rather than maintaining parallel prose copies or adding another summary. Keep character-local knowledge and narrator-only style out of the router. Preserve the original rules-neutral generic template and keep One-Star authority story-local or in a modular adapter. Measure the exact rendered stable prefix before and after, and retain volatile actor, participant, and turn data only after the user delimiter.

The exact begin router system prefix is materially smaller than 107,697 characters while preserving summon, synthesis, promotion, lethality, visibility, floor-exit, and Master-interface adjudication. Binding permutations still produce byte-identical system messages and only semantic participant differences in user tails. Offline behavioral and negative prompt-hygiene tests cover the retained contracts without asserting approved prose. No new summary block duplicates canonical or seed authority.

Preserve the defer marker in compact router history where it provides pacing feedback, but do not expose the directive to prose composition.
acceptance_criteria: A defer turn never emits or paraphrases the literal directive as player fiction. Any visible pause or ensuing pressure comes only from canonical facts, while ordinary player actions remain present in narrator input. title: Preserve second person inside canonical direct speech
description: Rowan said 'You counted the exits too,' addressing Renna. Router canonicalization rewrote quoted 'you' into a bracketed Renna id, and narration produced the awkward 'Renna Holt counted the exits too, or was Renna Holt...' A broad pronoun-normalization rule intended to make actor references explicit is modifying the semantic and voice of exact dialogue.
design: Keep direct speech verbatim apart from narrowly reviewed text-safety normalization. Resolve ambiguous first-person and second-person references only in surrounding canonical description or explicit structured source and target fields; never mechanically replace pronouns inside quotes. Preserve addressee semantics through observer and routing metadata rather than rewriting the utterance.
acceptance_criteria: A character saying 'You counted the exits too' remains exactly that in canonical facts and narrator input while the addressee is still unambiguous from structured context. Tests cover quoted first and second person, unquoted action prose needing explicit ids, nested punctuation, and no regression to raw-id resolution or player-controller leakage.

Do not send broader hidden lore and then ask the model to ignore it. Add bounded semantic validation or retry for obvious references outside the grant, while keeping low-cognition D&D combat-spawn work in ayoa-se0 and avoiding game-specific assumptions in generic generation.
acceptance_criteria: A tier-one One-Star summon cannot know synthesis, later facilities, hidden economy rules, or other unrevealed concepts, but can use all explicitly sanctioned Master/Tower/gate knowledge. Higher-tier or explicitly informed characters retain their authored knowledge. Rendered generation prompts contain no disallowed lore for the tier; offline fixtures cover allowed knowledge, obvious excess/retry, private-record persistence, and non-One-Star isolation.

title: Diversify One-Star summons and teach the silent-Master contract
description: The generated opening wave in one-star-human-test was superficially distinct but behaviorally homogeneous: Dara becomes quieter under pressure, Bram also becomes quieter, and Pell becomes stiller. All three remained composed enough to coordinate cautiously, then repeatedly waited instead of driving the mission. Strengthen the One-Star-specific tier-one generation guidance so fresh summons vary materially in fear response, compliance, initiative, social strategy, and willingness to fight. Some summons should comply, while others may refuse, argue, freeze, collapse in panic, flee, or require coercion; these possibilities should create story pressure without making every wave dysfunctional. Give newly summoned Heroes a standard in-fiction orientation from Iselle before deployment: they serve a silent Master who can hear an observed Hero but cannot answer, deployed Heroes must act for themselves, and refusal carries serious but initially unknown consequences. Keep this authored to One-Star Ascension rather than adding gacha assumptions to generic character agents.
acceptance_criteria: One-Star generation guidance requires materially different pressure and compliance profiles within a multi-summon wave and does not permit three variants of quiet watchfulness to satisfy diversity. Iselle delivers the shared silent-Master, autonomous-mission, and uncertain-consequence orientation to every fresh summon through one coherent scene or equivalent canonical observation before deployment. Character-agent context retains what each Hero actually heard, so an autonomous Hero does not wait for an impossible tactical reply. Controlled multi-wave generation/playtest coverage demonstrates both functional cooperation and credible refusal, panic, collapse, argument, or attempted noncompliance across the sample without requiring those behaviors in every wave. Tests validate rendered/context contracts and forbidden leakage without freezing approved prose.

title: Benchmark FLUX.2-dev references and regional scene assembly
description: Run a controlled evaluation on the pinned four-MI210 FLUX.2-dev service to determine the minimum and useful maximum number of references for consistently good solo, multi-character, enemy, and architecture scenes. Compare direct whole-scene generation against output-side regional workflows: masked regional prompting/attention coupling on one shared canvas, independent character/background passes composited as layers, and a final low-denoise inpaint or harmonization pass that unifies lighting, depth, contact shadows, and seams. Verify FLUX.2-dev compatibility before adopting any ComfyUI regional node intended for older FLUX variants.
design: Treat reference count and scene-assembly method as separate experimental axes. Baseline direct FLUX.2-dev first. Regional path: assign each subject and the shared environment an explicit mask/region while preserving shared-canvas denoising. Composite path: generate the environment and each identity-critical subject independently with scene-matched pose/camera/lighting, alpha-mask and place them with correct scale/depth, then run a restrained whole-image harmonization or seam inpaint without allowing identity drift. Include feathering/context overlap and denoise-strength ablations. Do not modify production bindings or orchestration until human review.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible benchmark records model revision, reference hashes, prompts, seeds, steps, guidance, latency, and peak VRAM; screens direct generation with 1 through 6 references; compares at least one shared-canvas regional-conditioning workflow and one generate-separate-parts/composite/harmonize workflow; scores identity fidelity, costume/prop fidelity, cross-subject leakage, exact subject count, anatomy, interaction/contact quality, composition, architecture adherence, seam/cutout artifacts, and global lighting/style coherence; includes solo identity, two- and three-character scenes, character-plus-enemy action, and establishing architecture; uses enough repeated seeds on finalists to support a practical consistency claim; and ends with a concrete recommendation for Ayoa reference limits and when to use direct, regional, or composited generation.
notes: Clarification: output paneling means regional generation or multi-pass compositing, not concatenating several input references into one panel. Current facts remain: BFL recommends at most 6 references for FLUX.2-dev; the deployed server accepts 6; Ayoa currently caps requests at 4. Research should distinguish regional attention conditioning from genuinely independent layer generation and later compositing.

title: Improve asynchronous image-generation UX
description: Why this exists: higher-quality FLUX.2 Klein Base generation takes roughly 30-50 seconds per illustration on the RTX 3090. Discord delivery is backgrounded, but CLI currently waits after each command and players receive limited progress/order feedback. What needs to be done: design and implement a more asynchronous frontend experience that preserves canonical turn speed and POV privacy while keeping generated images ordered and rewind-safe. Evaluate immediate prose plus queued-image acknowledgements, nonblocking CLI input/redraw, job status/progress surfaces, late-delivery ordering, queue backpressure/coalescing, warm worker lifecycle, cancellation, and failure messaging. Acceptance criteria: players can continue interacting while images generate; completed images are delivered to the correct POV and source turn in order; rewind/session detach suppress stale work; busy/failure states are clear without blocking story turns; offline concurrency tests cover Discord and CLI behavior.
notes: Live CLI resummon test confirmed the director generated four valid requests and prose gates opened, but the user saw no immediate feedback while jobs sat behind a forgotten two-day-old CLI that still held the global GPU/queue lock. Once the stale owner was stopped, the current Base+LoRA worker drained and delivered all four jobs. Add visible queued/busy owner status and progress acknowledgment so a fired director cannot look like a skip, and consider detecting/reporting stale-version queue owners.

title: Evaluate router-triggered content manager callback
description: Why this exists: live Lost Laboratory playtesting showed the content manager currently runs on a fixed preflight interval, which can call too early, too late, or during turns where only the router can know it lacks imported-content context. The team wants to evaluate whether content-manager invocation should instead act like a router-requested callback or mixed trigger. What needs to be done: compare the current timer/preflight model with a router-triggered content lookup callback design, including latency, retry behavior, prompt/input contracts, deterministic validation, and whether the router can request keys without seeing excessive catalog context. Acceptance criteria: a concrete recommendation exists for timer-only, router-callback-only, or hybrid behavior; the recommendation names the exact runtime loop, failure handling, and model inputs for Lost Laboratory-style imported modules and larger modules like Strahd.
notes: Filed before continuing the default-interval soak. Related evidence: app/storage/playtest_reports/lost_laboratory_default_cm_soak_20260527T154259Z/partial_report.json restored content_manager_refresh_interval from 999 to 3; content manager ran once at start and subsequent preflight skips/cadence reinforce the callback-vs-timer question.

title: Sync active D&D combat HP back to character mechanics
description: Why this exists: Lost Laboratory continuation reports show active_combat HP diverging from character mechanics. At app/storage/playtest_reports/lost_laboratory_player_continuation_20260526T162336Z, Marlowe is 15/24 HP in session.active_combat while resource_state_after still reports mechanics hit_points current 24/24 and temporary 0. The same run demonstrates some resource writes do sync, because Ilyra's Healing Word slot reached spell_slot_1 3/4. If combat later ends with mechanics HP stale, exploration, sheets, rest logic, and future encounters will start from the wrong state. What needs to be done: define and implement the D&D adapter sync boundary for HP, temp HP, conditions, and active effects between active combat participants and durable character mechanics.
acceptance_criteria: When active D&D combat mutates PC HP/temp HP/conditions/effects, durable character mechanics either stay in sync during combat or are reconciled exactly once on combat end; /sheet and resource_state do not show full HP after combat damage; regression covers damage, healing, temp HP, and combat-end transition without duplicating resource spends.

title: Show D&D XP awards once per defeated combatant

title: Roll and surface healing dice in D&D combat auto-rolls

Player auto-roll mode should still produce code-owned healing dice when a spell has a healing formula, and those dice should be visible before narration just like attack and damage rolls. acceptance_criteria: Healing Word or another healing spell in active D&D combat with auto-roll enabled records a healing die result in the dice ledger, applies HP from that rolled result plus modifiers, surfaces the roll in CLI output before prose, and spends the spell slot exactly once. Regression should fail if the resolver applies an averaged or unrolled healing formula.

title: Validate combat-manager damage ledgers before applying HP changes
description: Lost Laboratory soak reports show the combat resolver trusting invalid combat-manager roll ledgers. 20260524T144931Z showed a Mountain Lion claw hit applying both the attack damage entry and a separate damage_roll entry from the same resolved attack, for 9 total slashing. 20260525T204545Z resumed to ckpt_0060 showed a mace attack that missed Gearbox (9 vs AC 12) but still emitted/applied 5 bludgeoning, reducing Gearbox from 22 to 17, and a PC longsword hit applying duplicate damage entries to the Bandit Captain. Investigate whether output shape should forbid invalid damage records and add deterministic validation/deduplication so damage is only applied for legal hit/effect outcomes.

The fallback should not infer loot from tack, existing inventory use, or ordinary handling of owned gear.

Acceptance: player-facing prose uses display names for spawned/implicit NPCs and respects attached D&D identity/species in narrator and NPC dialogue context.
notes: Implemented narrator guidance to convert underscore raw identifiers into best-guess display names. NPC dialogue ancestry/species grounding remains outstanding and should be handled separately.
close_reason: D&D identity/species now reaches narrator and NPC-agent user context only in D&D mode, preventing wrong ancestry references without leaking into non-D&D prompts; context tests pass.

title: Bridge narrative gear acquisition into D&D inventory or loot
description: In CLI playtest cli_takeover_haiku_20260520, Korva visibly issued rope, bedrolls, rations, torches, waterskins, food parcels, and a healer's kit. /loot stayed empty and /inventory still showed only the imported D&D Beyond equipment. From a D&D perspective, gear acquisition should either create a loot offer, update carried inventory, or explicitly tell the player it is narrative-only. Acceptance: when router/narrator awards mundane adventuring gear in a D&D session, the CLI exposes a structured inventory/loot path or a clear non-inventory explanation; /loot all should be testable on this path.
close_reason: Added a D&D-only narrative mundane gear handoff fallback that creates claimable loot offers for obvious visible supplies, strengthened router loot guidance, and tested /loot-all style claiming through inventory.

title: Add non-combat D&D checks for risky scouting and parley

Risky scouting/listening/stealth/recon and tense parley all resolved as Cat I prose with no pending /roll prompts: Garrick scouted the mill, counted seven armed brigands, and found a covered lane; Lyra approached under cover and negotiated with a drawn bow on her, but no Stealth/Perception/Insight/Persuasion check fired. From a D&D table perspective these are obvious ability-check moments. Acceptance: D&D adapter can request interactive player rolls for non-combat exploration/social Cat II uncertainty without forcing initiative, and CLI /roll can resolve them into visible prose.
close_reason: Duplicate of ayoa-6x1; 2026-05-20 CLI rerun evidence appended there.

title: Design cumulative synthesis personality and morality fusion
description: Deferred design work for whether repeated synthesis should leave cumulative memories, mannerisms, moral injury, or identity bleed in the surviving Hero. This is deliberately outside the deterministic bookkeeping implementation so the current adapter does not invent character psychology.
design: Preserve the LLM-backed character as the authority for subjective portrayal. Explore a compact durable, visibility-scoped semantic record of source influence that can be introduced through witnessed fiction rather than numeric personality fusion. Avoid exposing hidden source memories to Master, router, or target before fiction establishes them.
acceptance_criteria: A reviewed design defines what survives synthesis, who can know it, how it accumulates, how agents receive it, and how it avoids deterministic personality replacement; implementation is separately approved before code changes.

title: Do not persist surface-empty canonical events
description: Event 80 routed Renna for a reaction, received an entirely internal response, then appended a canonical event with no observable facts and no observers before closing. Event 68's rationale called for observation_harvest but schema coercion stored cascade_exhausted because there was no enrichment target. These records add history and calls without any canonical surface and obscure whether a beat changed.
design: When an agent submission contains only private interior material and yields no observable fact, lifecycle change, commitment, location, mission or status update, or other canonical side effect, close or continue from the prior real event without appending a fake empty event. Keep the private character history where appropriate. Require diagnostic kind and rationale to match the accepted schema outcome rather than relying on silent coercion.
acceptance_criteria: An internal-only agent response creates no empty canonical event, no visibility-log entry, no narrator/image receipt, and no compact prior_event while preserving the character's private conversation. A genuinely silent but externally observable pause can still be canonicalized. Tests cover internal thought, visible nonverbal action, enrichment with/without a target, and checkpoint/history counts.

Low priority; investigate whether the router occasionally attaches off-location observers to intimate Cat I beats and tighten if it recurs.

title: Represent hit-gated bonus damage dependencies explicitly
description: While fixing ayoa-5d3, the observed bad ledgers were same-source duplicates and are now normalized away. A separate future rules gap remains for distinct feature damage that should happen only if a specific attack roll hits, such as class-feature or spell riders. The current damage_roll shape has no dependency on an attack roll, so representing these as direct damage_rolls would make them unconditional and risk damage after a miss.
acceptance_criteria: Combat plan schema can represent bonus/rider damage that depends on a specific attack_roll without relying on reason text. Validation rejects or strips dependent damage when the attack misses before HP mutation. Regression covers a miss with a distinct-source hit-gated rider and a hit that applies the rider exactly once.

title: Support stationary imported combatants
description: Imported D&D combat statblocks currently require at least one positive movement mode, which forced the Lost Laboratory brain-in-jar runtime record to use minimal synthetic movement even though the reviewed source presents it as effectively stationary unless moved by machinery or a carrier. Add an explicit stationary combatant representation or relax validation so speed 0 records can still enter combat when their actions and placement are valid.
acceptance_criteria: A reviewed imported statblock with all movement modes at 0 can resolve into combat state without synthetic speed, remains unable to move unless an effect grants movement, and existing positive-speed statblock validation still catches missing speed fields.
close_reason: Completed: imported statblocks now allow explicit zero-speed combatants while still rejecting missing or empty speed fields; regression covers stationary character, combatant, and monster projections.

title: Add safe map and image reveal pipeline for content packs
description: Implement the image/map side of adventure content lookup. Runtime should refer to private image assets by safe refs, reveal only player-safe derivatives/captions according to observer visibility, and keep source pages, raw bytes, local paths, and player-hidden labels out of narrator/agent/player surfaces. The omniscient router may receive reviewed authored map/secret/asset facts as structured text when needed; it still never receives source images or raw source artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Revealed asset refs are filtered per POV for CLI and Discord; private image refs and source paths never leak to narrators, agents, player output, logs, or default checkpoints; router-facing asset/map context is reviewed authored text/structure only, not image analysis or raw source paths; rewind restores reveal/fog state; tests cover two observers seeing different safe asset visibility for the same event.
notes: 2026-05-21 implementation wave landed safe asset catalog/reveal filtering in commit c1651ca: player-safe asset records, redacted delivery refs/captions, per-POV AssetReveal filtering, and tests for differing observer visibility without raw paths/protected excerpts. Remaining before full issue closure: durable reveal/fog checkpoint state, CLI/Discord delivery integration, rewind coverage, and no-public-fallback behavior for private delivery failures.
close_reason: Verified safe map/image reveal pipeline: per-POV CLI/Discord delivery, private failure withholding, safe asset payload filtering, and rewind-restored reveal/fog state all pass.
